# Turkey Blocks Social Media Sites Over Images of Prosecutor Hostage Crisis

Turkey has temporarily blocked access to Facebook, Twitter, and YouTube after the social media platforms shared images of a prosecutor being held at gunpoint during a hostage crisis at an Istanbul courthouse.

The blocks on Facebook and Twitter were later lifted after they both complied with government demands. Talks with YouTube are continuing. Two gunmen, reportedly from a far-left group, took prosecutor Mehmet Selim Kiraz hostage at an Istanbul courthouse last week. All three died during a police rescue bid.

Turkish officials described the images of the prosecutor as "anti-government propaganda" and moved swiftly to prevent their distribution. Before imposing the blocks on the websites, Turkish authorities had already moved to stop newspapers from printing the images. The newspapers were accused by the government of disseminating "terrorist propaganda" for the DHKP-C group that was reportedly behind the attack on the courthouse. The DHKP-C is considered a terrorist group by Turkey, the European Union and the United States.

Mr Kiraz was apparently taken hostage because he headed an investigation into the 2013 death of a boy during anti-government protests. The pictures showing attackers holding a gun to his head were being widely shared on social media, prompting authorities to act.

"The wife and children of prosecutor Kiraz have been deeply upset. The images are everywhere," a senior Turkish official told the Reuters news agency. In total, 166 websites which shared the images were blocked by court order.

Millions of social media users tried to access their favourite platforms but with no success. However, the block did not stop people from attempting to communicate. Newspapers and individuals alike shared guidelines on how to circumvent the ban. The hashtag #TwitterisblockedinTurkey became the number one trending topic worldwide.

Facebook was subject to the same block but restrictions were lifted after it removed the images before the expiration of a deadline imposed by the court. Twitter reacted more slowly and access to the messaging system was blocked for several hours on Monday. YouTube published the text of the court ruling on its website saying an "administration measure" had been enacted by Turkey's telecoms authority, adding it was seeking ways to restore access.

This is not the first time that Turkish authorities have imposed blocks on social media sites and networks. The Turkish government has a complicated relationship with social media platforms. In the run-up to local elections in March 2014, blocks were imposed after recordings circulated allegedly revealing corruption among senior officials. The then prime minister, now President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, described Twitter as a menace to society.

Figures provided by Twitter revealed that Turkey filed more requests to remove content from the social network than any other nation between July and December 2014. With general elections scheduled for 7 June and tensions running high, many people fear similar bans on social platforms could follow.

# Cardinal Pell Admits He "Should Have Done More" About Paedophile Priest

Cardinal George Pell has admitted he "should have done more" after learning of allegations against a paedophile priest in 1974, during his testimony to an Australian Royal Commission investigating institutional responses to child sexual abuse.

The cardinal told the commission, which is conducting hearings in Rome, that a student at St Patrick's College in Ballarat informed him that Brother Edward Dowlan was "misbehaving with boys" in 1974. However, Cardinal Pell said the information was "casually mentioned" and claimed the boy did not explicitly ask him to take action.

Dowlan, who has since changed his name to Ted Bales, was jailed last year for abusing boys throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Cardinal Pell is giving evidence via video link from Rome after being excused from returning to Australia due to a heart condition.

## Survivors Confront Cardinal's Testimony

A group of abuse survivors and their supporters have traveled to Rome to face Australia's most senior Catholic as he testifies. Among them is Peter Blenkiron, who was abused by Brother Dowlan and spoke shortly after the cardinal's admission.

"That's me in 1973, six months before I went to St Patrick's," Mr Blenkiron said, pointing to a photograph on his T-shirt. "If action would've been taken, that little boy wouldn't have gone through what he went through."

Cardinal Pell described it as a "disastrous coincidence" that five paedophiles came to be at the same school and parish in Ballarat during the 1970s. This characterization angered abuse survivor Stephen Wood, who has previously disclosed being bashed and molested starting from age 11. "Coincidence my foot, it was clearly systemic," he said.

## Bribery Allegations Denied

The cardinal also denied allegations that he attempted to bribe the nephew of notorious paedophile priest Gerald Ridsdale. David Ridsdale, who was abused by his uncle, has claimed that Cardinal Pell offered him money to "keep quiet." The inquiry heard that David Ridsdale initially avoided involving police because he feared his grandmother would discover his uncle's actions.

On the eve of Cardinal Pell's final day of testimony, David Ridsdale expressed hope that the group's request to meet with Pope Francis would be approved. "Most likely we will meet with Cardinal Pell and we have a good chance of a Papal meeting on Friday," he said. "We want an understanding and an acknowledgment this is a global systemic problem."

Cardinal Pell released a statement offering to meet victims in small groups without lawyers or media present, and said he would be "happy to assist with requests to meet Pope Francis."

# Passenger Restrained on British Airways Flight to Boston

A British Airways flight from London to Boston was met by police on Tuesday after a female passenger was restrained by crew members during the flight.

An airline spokesman told the BBC that reports of a passenger trying to access the cockpit were incorrect and they were not particularly concerned. Police met the plane upon landing at Boston's Logan Airport on Tuesday. The 30-year-old woman was restrained by the crew during the flight, the FAA said.

The six-and-half-hour Flight BA 213 originated from London's Heathrow Airport. British Airways officials said they believe the woman was intoxicated and they did not believe the incident was related to terrorism.

"We do not tolerate abusive behaviour," a statement said.

Earlier on Tuesday, four passengers were removed from a Baltimore to Chicago flight because of "suspicious behaviour". The incidents come as authorities have been put on heightened alert after devastating gun and suicide attacks killed at least 129 people in Paris.

# Russia Denies US Claims of Supplying Taliban in Afghanistan

Russia has firmly denied American allegations that it is supplying weapons to the Taliban in Afghanistan, dismissing the claims as "absolutely false" and designed to cover up US failures in the region.

The denial came after General Curtis Scaparrotti, Nato's Supreme Allied Commander in Europe, told US lawmakers in Washington on Thursday that Moscow was "perhaps" supplying the extremist group. However, he provided no evidence to support the serious allegation.

Zamir Kabulov, the Kremlin's special envoy in Afghanistan, responded swiftly on Friday, telling RIA Novosti state news agency that the accusations were fabrications. "These fabrications are designed, as we have repeatedly underlined, to justify the failure of the US military and politicians in the Afghan campaign. There is no other explanation," he said.

The allegations represent a significant point of tension in an already complicated relationship between Russia and the Taliban. Russia officially considers the Taliban a terrorist organisation and historically backed the Northern Alliance against the group during Afghanistan's civil war in the 1990s. Moscow has previously stated that its limited contact with the Taliban is aimed at bringing them to the negotiating table.

However, Russia's approach toward the Afghan Taliban has softened dramatically over the past year. In December 2015, Russian officials conceded that "the Taliban interest objectively coincides with ours" in the fight against so-called Islamic State. Several Russian officials have since publicly acknowledged Moscow's "contacts" with the Taliban.

Russian authorities cite two main reasons for these contacts: ensuring the security of Russian citizens and political offices in Taliban-controlled areas, and countering IS, which established its regional branch in Afghanistan in January 2015. The Taliban's assurances that it will prevent IS from reaching Russia's borders and those of regional players like Iran and China have been particularly valued by Moscow.

During his Senate Armed Services Committee hearing, Gen Scaparrotti stated: "I've seen the influence of Russia of late - increased influence in terms of association and perhaps even supply to the Taliban," but offered no additional details.

High-ranking American military officials have accused Russia of undermining the Afghan government and its US/Nato allies by "legitimizing" the Taliban. Western officials also claim Russia is using IS's emergence in Afghanistan as an excuse for meddling in the country.

Afghan officials have urged Moscow to work with the government rather than establishing links with non-state actors for regional peace and stability.

# Apple Faces Price-Fixing Restrictions Following E-Book Antitrust Ruling

Apple has been hit with new restrictions on its e-book business following a landmark court decision on price-fixing allegations. The move follows a court ruling in July that Apple conspired with five publishers to control e-book prices.

The judge also ordered Apple to hire an external monitor to ensure it complies with the new rules. The US Department of Justice, which launched legal action against Apple, said it was "pleased" with the outcome.

Under the new restrictions, Apple is now not allowed to enter agreements with the five publishers that would allow prices to be fixed. The judgement expires after five years, though the judge can order extensions if necessary.

"We're pleased that the court has issued an order supporting the Department of Justice's efforts to address Apple's illegal price fixing conduct," said assistant attorney general Bill Baer in a statement. "Consumers will continue to benefit from lower e-books prices as a result of the department's enforcement action to restore competition in this important industry."

Apple was found to have encouraged publishers to set the price of their e-books, rather than allowing retailers to decide the price. Prosecutors said this was aimed at Amazon - a rival e-book retailer that charged lower prices than Apple was able to offer.

As a result, Amazon's typical price of $9.99 (£6.39) for a best-seller rose to $12.99 or $14.99 after the launch of the iPad, they said.

The publishers involved were Hachette Book Group, HarperCollins, Holtzbrinck - which does business as Macmillan, Penguin Group and Simon & Schuster.

# Tunisia's Government to Step Down After Three-Week Talks

Tunisia's Islamist-led government has agreed to resign and make way for a caretaker administration, potentially ending a political crisis that has threatened the country's democratic transition.

The decision marks a breakthrough in weeks of tensions between the ruling coalition, led by the Islamist Ennahda party, and the secular opposition. It is hoped a caretaker government will be negotiated over the next three weeks that will prepare for new elections.

The talks were announced on Saturday by the powerful UGTT labour union, which will act as a mediator. The union urged both sides to set a date for next week to begin negotiations.

Under the deal, the Ennahda party has agreed to three weeks of talks, after which it will hand power to an independent transition leadership and set a date for parliamentary and presidential elections.

"The dialogue will start on Monday or Tuesday," said Lotfi Zitoun, an Ennahda party official, according to Reuters. "Ennahda has accepted the plan without conditions to get the country out of the political crisis."

The crisis has threatened to disrupt a transition to democracy that began after Tunisians threw out their decades-old authoritarian government at the beginning of the 2011 Arab Spring uprisings.

Anti-government protests intensified recently after the killing of two opposition figures. The murders of opposition politician Mohammed Brahmi in July and Chokri Belaid, a prominent leftist, in February have deepened political divisions.

The opposition has accused the Ennahda party of pushing an Islamist agenda in the previously secular nation. Before the 2011 ousting of Tunisia's longtime leader, Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali, the country had been known as one of the most secular in the Arab world.

The moderate Islamist government has blamed hardliners for the killings, but the National Salvation Front-led opposition has accused Ennahda of failing to rein in radical Islamists.

While Tunisia's uprising spread through the Arab world, efforts to strengthen democracy at home have stalled due to political antagonism. Analysts say the talks could struggle to break a deadlock if the rival parties are unable to overcome differences over a new constitution and the running of elections.

# Ardbeg Whisky Reaches for the Stars with Space Experiment

A Scottish distillery has launched an out-of-this-world experiment, sending whisky compounds into orbit to study how space affects the aging process.

Ardbeg, the renowned Islay distillery, blasted vials of chemical compounds to the International Space Station last year aboard a Soyuz rocket from Kazakhstan. The micro-organic compounds are spending up to two years interacting with charred oak in near zero gravity conditions, in what is believed to be the first experiment of its kind.

The groundbreaking research, conducted in partnership with Texas-based space research company NanoRacks, went live in January when scientists broke the separating wall between the experimental components. Results will be compared with a control sample currently maturing at Ardbeg's earthbound distillery.

Dr Bill Lumsden, director of distilling and whisky creation at Ardbeg, expressed optimism about the project. "So far so good," he said. "We will not know the results for another year or so but in the meantime we thought we would celebrate the experiment by the introduction of Ardbeg Galileo."

The limited edition 12-year-old single malt whisky, named Ardbeg Galileo in honor of the space experiment, is a vatting of different Ardbeg styles laid down in 1999.

The vials launched into space contain terpenes, a class of chemical compounds crucial to whisky's flavor profile. Ardbeg hopes the experiment will reveal how these large, complex molecules behave in near zero gravity, potentially uncovering new chemical building blocks in their flavor spectrum.

The research could have applications beyond whisky production, potentially benefiting various commercial and research products. Ardbeg was invited to participate in the innovative two-year experiment in late 2011, marking a unique intersection of traditional whisky-making and cutting-edge space science.

# Lalchand Rajput Named Afghanistan Cricket Coach

Indian cricket veteran Lalchand Rajput has been appointed as Afghanistan's new head coach, the Afghanistan Cricket Board announced today.

The 54-year-old reportedly edged out former Pakistan batsman Mohammad Yousuf and ex-South Africa opener Herschelle Gibbs for the prestigious position. Rajput brings extensive coaching experience, having managed India's victorious 2007 World Twenty20 campaign and led Mumbai Indians in the Indian Premier League. He has also worked with India's Under-19 and A teams.

Rajput, who played two Tests and four ODIs for India between 1985 and 1987, replaces Pakistan legend Inzamam-ul-Haq, who resigned in April to become Pakistan's chief selector. Rajput will commence his tenure during Afghanistan's upcoming tour of Scotland, Ireland and the Netherlands in July and August.

Afghanistan Cricket Board chairman Nasimullah Danish expressed confidence in the appointment, stating: "Mr Rajput is technically and professionally strong coach in cricket. I am sure his presence with Afghan national cricket team will be of benefit."

# Nigeria Probes Discovery of $135,000 in Cash at Kaduna Airport

Nigerian anti-corruption authorities are investigating after discovering 49 million naira (approximately $135,000) in suspicious circumstances at Kaduna airport.

The cash, in the local naira currency, was found near the airport's check-in area and was still in sealed packs. An investigation is under way to trace the source of the money, a spokesman for Nigeria's Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) says.

Tackling corruption was a key election pledge for President Muhammadu Buhari.

"Operatives [of the EFCC] intercepted a sum of 49m naira in five large black 150kg sacks following a tip off," the EFCC said on its website. It added that investigations are "in top gear" to find the "culprits behind the attempted illegal movement of the cash".

EFCC official Ibrahim Bappah said the cash haul, made up of "crispy naira notes", was discovered on Tuesday when airport security detected a distinctive aroma during a routine screening.

It is not known where the cash was being sent, and the EFCC has said it is looking into whether the money is linked to any crime.

The discovery fits into a pattern of cash seizures by the anti-graft team. In February, the EFCC seized nearly $1.75m in cash at a house belonging to the former boss of the country's giant oil firm. In another case, a corruption probe against former petroleum minister Diezani Alison-Madueke resulted in a federal high court directing the confiscation of $150m.

Nigerians are keen to know who left the bundles of crispy notes and what they planned to do with the cash.

# Millions in England May Be Deficient in Vitamin D, Health Body Warns

Around 10 million people across England could be deficient in vitamin D, with many unaware of their condition, according to new guidance from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE).

The NHS advisory body has published a report calling for urgent action to address the deficiency, which can lead to serious health problems including rickets in children and brittle bones in adults. The recommendations include providing free vitamin D supplements to children and encouraging supermarkets to stock low-cost tablets.

Official estimates suggest that one in five adults and one in six children in England may have low levels of the essential vitamin. The problem is particularly acute among certain populations, with nearly 75% of adults from Asian, African, and Caribbean backgrounds potentially affected during winter months due to darker skin requiring more sunlight exposure.

Professor Mike Kelly, who helped develop the NICE guidelines, warned: "Around 10 million people in England may have low vitamin D status and so could be at risk of health problems - and they may not know it. People with darker skin are particularly at risk."

Unlike most vitamins, which are primarily obtained through diet, people get the majority of their vitamin D from sunlight exposure on the skin. However, the limited sunlight during British winter months means residents must rely on stores built up during summer, making supplementation crucial for at-risk groups.

The chief medical officer in England has already urged doctors to prescribe tablets to vulnerable populations, with similar advice issued across Northern Ireland, Wales, and Scotland. However, experts remain concerned that many people are still not receiving adequate vitamin D.

NICE's recommendations include several practical measures: local authorities should provide free tablets to children, manufacturers should ensure supplements are sold at the recommended dose of 10 micrograms daily for adults, and supermarkets should stock affordable options while promoting them to at-risk customers.

Healthcare professionals are also encouraged to discuss and record vitamin D intake with vulnerable patients at every opportunity.

Professor Susan Jebb, involved in developing the guidance, emphasized: "It is really important health professionals are aware of the problem and that everyone understands that for those at risk of deficiency, a good diet alone will not solve the issue."

Those at risk can purchase supplements over-the-counter or consult their GPs for advice.

# Kraft Heinz Reports Major Loss After Merger

Food giant Kraft Heinz has reported a net loss of $303m (£199m) in the third quarter of 2015, a dramatic decline from the $8m loss recorded the previous year.

The substantial loss comes after Kraft and Heinz completed their merger in July. Since combining operations, the company has implemented aggressive cost-cutting measures, including significant workforce reductions.

On Wednesday, Kraft Heinz announced plans to eliminate an additional 2,600 jobs and close seven North American factories. These moves are part of a broader strategy to achieve $1.5bn in annual cost savings by the end of 2017.

Pro forma sales in the US declined, driven by falling demand for products including Capri Sun drinks and ready meals. The company's shares remained unchanged in after-hours trading Thursday.

Despite the substantial quarterly loss, Kraft Heinz demonstrated confidence in its future prospects by raising its dividend 4.5% to 57 cents per share.

# European Parliament Demands Release of Irish Teen Ibrahim Halawa Held in Egypt

The European Parliament has overwhelmingly passed a resolution calling for the immediate release of Ibrahim Halawa, an Irish citizen detained in Egypt since 2013. More than 560 MEPs voted in favour of the resolution, compared with 11 against.

The motion was raised by Irish politicians criticising the Egyptian government's treatment of Mr Halawa. He was arrested aged 17 during a siege on the Al-Fath mosque in Cairo in 2013, and could face the death penalty.

The possibility of a death sentence for Mr Halawa, who was a minor at the time of his arrest, was criticised by the resolution. The motion said that capital punishment for a minor was a violation of international human rights law.

Egyptian authorities alleged that Mr Halawa attended two illegal protests on 16 and 17 August 2013 during a family holiday. He has strongly denied the charges and said he was taking refuge from violent clashes between security forces and protestors in the Cairo mosque.

Now aged 20, Mr Halawa's trial was postponed for the tenth time on 15 December. His case is being heard alongside 493 other defendants, a move that his legal counsel have said constitutes a violation of his human rights. His next trial date is 19 December.

The European Parliament's resolution makes a number of criticisms of the Egyptian government's treatment of Mr Halawa. The European Parliament said it was deeply concerned about the "unacceptable breach of basic human rights."

Mr Halawa's solicitor said they were "delighted" at the European Parliament's move. "The resolution signifies the context of Ibrahim's detention against the wider backdrop of human rights abuses in Egypt, and the continuing failure to uphold the very basic human rights enshrined in international law," he said.

Mr Halawa's legal team have raised concerns about his treatment during his time in custody, alleging that his human rights have been violated. They maintain that he endured torture, inhumane treatment and was denied access to his legal counsel.

Mr Halawa was on a family holiday to Egypt when he and his three sisters were arrested during a crackdown on protestors in the country's capital. His sisters were allowed to return to Dublin in November 2013.

# Castle Douglas Gallery Showcases Local Artists' Food and Drink-Themed Exhibition

Paintings, jewellery, woodwork, photography and ceramics are among the artworks by mainly local artists on display in Castle Douglas.

The exhibition at the McGill Duncan Gallery runs until 23 April.

# Celtic to Take Time Finding New Manager After Deila Exit

Celtic have pledged to conduct a thorough search for their next manager following Ronny Deila's departure from the club.

The Scottish champions released a short statement following news of talks with Malky Mackay and Brendan Rodgers. David Moyes, Roy Keane, Paul Lambert and Neil Lennon have also been strongly linked with the vacancy.

# Venezuela Swears In Nicolas Maduro as Acting President After Chavez's Death

CARACAS, Venezuela - Nicolas Maduro has been sworn in as acting president of Venezuela, taking over leadership following the death of Hugo Chavez earlier this week.

The ceremony was led by National Assembly Speaker Diosdado Cabello in the capital, Caracas. Mr Chavez, who died on 5 March after a long battle with cancer, had named Mr Maduro as his chosen successor.

However, the main opposition coalition boycotted Mr Maduro's swearing-in, saying that it was unconstitutional. It argues that - under the constitution - the speaker of the National Assembly should be the one to take over as acting president. The opposition leader, Henrique Capriles, called the move fraudulent.

After swearing in Mr Maduro, Mr Cabello said: "Venezuela will follow the route to socialism." As acting president, Mr Maduro is expected to call elections within 30 days.

Holding a copy of the Venezuelan constitution in his hand, Mr Maduro announced at the National Assembly: "I swear in the name of absolute loyalty to Comandante [commander] Hugo Chavez that we will obey and defend this Bolivarian Constitution with the hard hand of the free people."

Fireworks exploded above Caracas as Maduro was sworn in.

Earlier on Friday, Venezuelans paid an emotional farewell to Hugo Chavez. Mr Maduro told mourners that Mr Chavez, who led Venezuela for 14 years, remained "undefeated, pure, living for all time."

The former vice-president began the funeral ceremony by presenting Mr Chavez's coffin with the sword of Simon Bolivar - the 19th-Century independence leader he claimed as his inspiration.

More than 30 world leaders attended the ceremony, including Cuban President Raul Castro, Iran's Mahmoud Ahmadinejad and Alexander Lukashenko of Belarus. A message was read out from Syrian President Bashar al-Assad.

# Study Links Light Drinking to Increased Cancer Risk, Particularly for Women

A major study published in the British Medical Journal has found that even light to moderate alcohol consumption may increase the risk of certain cancers, with the clearest link observed for breast cancer in women.

The research, which analyzed data from two large US studies involving more than 100,000 adults, has prompted health experts to reinforce existing advice that people should limit their alcohol intake and incorporate alcohol-free days into their weekly routine.

## Key Findings

The American studies defined light to moderate drinking as up to 15g of alcohol per day for women (equivalent to a small glass of wine) and up to 30g per day for men (approximately two 355ml bottles of beer).

For women, researchers found that the risk of alcohol-related cancers, predominantly breast cancer, increased even with just one alcoholic drink per day. The findings were less straightforward for men: no significant link was found among men who had never smoked, but current or former smokers who drank lightly or moderately showed an increased risk of certain cancers.

## Expert Reactions

Dr. Jurgen Rehm from the Centre for Addiction and Mental Health in Toronto, writing in an accompanying editorial, suggested that individuals with a family history of cancer "should consider reducing their intake to below recommended limits or even abstaining altogether, given the now well-established link between moderate drinking and alcohol-related cancers."

However, UK experts emphasized that the absolute risk for any individual light or moderate drinker remains relatively small. Sarah Williams, Cancer Research UK's health information manager, offered practical advice: "Cutting down on alcohol helps reduce the risk of cancer, so try having more alcohol-free days each week or swapping every other drink for something soft on a night out."

## Current Guidelines Under Review

The NHS currently recommends that men should not regularly exceed three to four units of alcohol daily (roughly two cans of 4.5% lager), while women should limit consumption to two to three units (about two small glasses of 12% wine). However, these drinking guidelines are currently under review and may be revised.

Cancer Research UK notes that while there is no guaranteed safe level of drinking, staying within recommended daily limits means the risks of harming health are low.

Dr. Richard Roope of the Royal College of GPs struck a balanced tone: "GPs do not want to be killjoys - but we want our patients to live long and healthy lives, and lifestyle habits, such as smoking and drinking alcohol, are very real risk factors in developing cancer that can't be ignored."

## Calls for Better Labeling

A Department of Health spokesman acknowledged that "drinking even small amounts of alcohol regularly can increase the risks of some health conditions," and confirmed that the Chief Medical Officer has assembled a group of experts to review current guidelines.

Prof. Sir Ian Gilmore, chairman of the Alcohol Health Alliance UK, has called for mandatory health warnings on alcohol labels to help consumers make informed choices. "We all have a right to know what we are putting into our bodies and, at the minute, consumers are being denied this right," he said.

The research adds to growing evidence linking alcohol consumption to cancer risk and underscores the importance of public awareness about the potential health impacts of drinking.

# Police Superintendent Condemns Metal Thieves Targeting Schools and Community Buildings

A senior police officer has expressed his anger and frustration after a primary school became the latest victim in a spate of metal thefts affecting vulnerable communities across South Wales.

Superintendent Simon Clarke of South Wales Police issued a stark warning following Thursday's theft at Tonypandy Primary School in Rhondda, where thieves stole part of the roof, causing approximately £20,000 in damage.

"I am so frustrated and angry," Supt Clarke told BBC Radio Wales. "The people committing these crimes have no ethics or morals because they are affecting the most vulnerable members of our community."

The incident is part of a wider problem affecting the region. Last year, figures obtained by BBC Wales revealed that metal thefts cost Welsh local authorities almost £680,000—more than double the previous year's total.

Supt Clarke emphasized that while police are implementing preventative measures including increased CCTV coverage and product marking schemes, community cooperation is essential to tackling the problem.

"I think the key actually lies with the communities because some people know who are doing these offences and we just need them to come forward," he said.

The superintendent expressed particular concern about the disparity between the minimal financial gain for thieves and the devastating impact on communities. "The financial return against a stolen piece of lead is minimal. The value of the lead or the tiles is very, very small," he explained. "Clearly, the physical damage is immense but it's far more than that. It's actually at the fabric of our community."

He warned that the consequences extend beyond immediate repair costs, noting that some village halls and community centres lack funds for repairs, leading to permanent closures that fragment communities.

"People should be outraged that yet again schools have been targeted," Supt Clarke added. "I saw and spoke to members of the community who were visibly upset that their schools have been damaged by the thoughtlessness and callousness of just a small minority."

The police are working closely with councils, health services, utility companies, and the Church in Wales to secure premises. However, Supt Clarke also called on scrap metal merchants to take responsibility.

"They cannot just say 'I didn't know'. They should be checking when they think something's a bit dodgy," he said. "If they weren't prepared to buy the products off the thieves, there would be no market."

# Porsche to Create 1,400 Jobs for Electric Sports Car Production

German luxury sports carmaker Porsche is embarking on an ambitious electric vehicle project, announcing 1,400 new positions as it races to bring its first battery-powered model to market by 2019.

The Volkswagen-owned manufacturer is investing approximately €1bn (£836m; $1.1bn) in the initiative, positioning itself to challenge Tesla's dominance in the electric sports car segment.

However, the company acknowledges significant recruitment challenges. "I'm not denying the battle for talent is tough," said Andreas Haffner, Porsche's human resources chief. "One can in fact describe what is going on now as a 'war for talents'."

Porsche faces stiff competition from rival automakers, suppliers, and technology firms globally. "Money alone is not enough to attract these creative minds," Haffner added.

The expansion comes as parent company VW works to recover from its diesel emissions scandal, having committed to launching 30 all-electric models as part of its transformation into a "green" transport leader.

The new positions will be located at Porsche's Zuffenhausen plant, adding to the company's existing workforce of over 24,000 employees.

# Scottish Episcopal Church Leader Responds to Controversy Over Koran Reading at Cathedral Service

The head of the Scottish Episcopal Church has addressed the growing controversy surrounding the reading of Islamic verses during an Epiphany service, whilst condemning the subsequent abuse directed at the cathedral involved.

The Most Rev David Chillingworth, the Church Primus and Bishop of St Andrews, Dunkeld and Dunblane, expressed deep distress over the widespread offence caused by the interfaith service at St Mary's Cathedral in Glasgow. In a blog post, he announced plans to convene those involved in interfaith relations to explore how such work can be carried forward respectfully, particularly regarding worship.

"The Scottish Episcopal Church is deeply distressed at the widespread offence which has been caused," Mr Chillingworth wrote. "We also deeply regret the widespread abuse which has been received by the cathedral community."

The controversy erupted after it emerged that passages from the Koran relating to the Virgin birth were read during Epiphany celebrations at the Kelvinbridge cathedral. Members of Glasgow's Muslim community had been invited to participate in the service, which was intended to promote understanding between faiths.

However, the inclusion of Islamic scripture provoked criticism from some quarters, particularly because Muslims regard Jesus as a prophet rather than the son of God - a fundamental theological difference with Christianity.

Police are now investigating offensive online messages directed at the cathedral following the service.

The cathedral's provost, the Very Rev Kelvin Holdsworth, defended the service in his Sunday sermon, describing it as an attempt to foster interfaith understanding. He revealed he had endured a "storm of abuse" from "10,000 'Christian' voices claiming to know what happened here that night."

"I would not have wished the week that I have had on anyone," Mr Holdsworth said. "The international hue and cry about our Epiphany service was not something anyone here was seeking."

He insisted that the service clearly proclaimed Christ's divinity and preached the Gospel, whilst enabling different faith communities to learn from one another. Mr Holdsworth also criticised what he termed "Islamophobic" responses and the "recently invigorated far-right media," arguing that moderate Western churches should not adopt policies of appeasement towards such voices.

The Primus emphasised that whilst decisions regarding the cathedral service were matters for the provost and cathedral community, the church remained committed to reconciliation. He stated the Scottish Episcopal Church's intention to bring together those involved in interfaith work to ensure future initiatives "command respect" and serve as "a worthy expression of the reconciliation to which all Christians are called."

The incident has raised broader questions about interfaith dialogue and worship practices in an increasingly connected world.

# Honda Changes Vandoorne's Engine After Electrical Problem at Spanish Test

Honda has been forced to replace the engine in Stoffel Vandoorne's McLaren on the opening day of Formula One's final pre-season test in Spain after discovering an electrical issue.

The Japanese manufacturer's latest setback comes amid a series of reliability concerns with its newly redesigned power unit. Honda used at least five engines during last week's initial pre-season test, raising questions about the reliability of the new specification.

Vandoorne completed the morning session in eighth position, finishing 2.972 seconds behind the pace-setter, before the team decided to swap the power unit.

A Honda spokeswoman explained the decision: "In the interests of maximising lap time, we opted to replace the power-unit and investigate the issue further once it is out of the car. The PU we are using is the same specification as the one run at the test last week."

Honda has confirmed it has an upgraded engine earmarked for the season-opening Australian Grand Prix on March 24-26, with expectations that the latest specification will be tested at some point this week at the Circuit de Catalunya-Barcelona.

Meanwhile, Williams driver Felipe Massa set the fastest time of the morning on super-soft tyres, finishing 0.174 seconds quicker than Red Bull's Daniel Ricciardo, who was using ultra-soft tyres.

Mercedes' Lewis Hamilton posted the third-fastest lap, 0.556 seconds behind Ricciardo, also on soft tyres. Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel was fourth, 0.671 seconds slower than Hamilton despite using the medium tyre compound, which Pirelli estimates to be 1.3-1.4 seconds slower than the soft tyre.

Direct comparison of lap times remains difficult as teams do not disclose fuel loads or specific car configurations, both of which significantly impact performance. Live text commentary of the test continues throughout the day.

# Grimsby Town Manager Paul Hurst Commits to Club Despite Speculation

Grimsby Town manager Paul Hurst has dismissed speculation linking him with other clubs and confirmed his commitment to The Mariners ahead of their FA Trophy final appearance.

The 41-year-old had been rumoured to be a target for Notts County following his success in guiding Grimsby back to the Football League after a six-year absence. However, Hurst has categorically ruled out any move away from Blundell Park.

"I genuinely have no other offers out there to even be in consideration," Hurst told BBC Radio Humberside. "There is nothing to tempt me. I've had a chat with the board, I've got a rough idea of what we're about and then set about building a squad that we can still be proud of."

The manager is currently focused on preparing his team for Sunday's FA Trophy final against FC Halifax Town at Wembley, which could cap a remarkable season for the club.

Hurst, who joined Grimsby in 2011 and became sole manager in 2013 after Rob Scott's dismissal for gross misconduct, has overseen four play-off campaigns in the National League. His persistence finally paid off when The Mariners defeated Forest Green Rovers 3-1 to secure promotion.

Despite some fan unrest during the campaign, Hurst acknowledged the importance of supporter backing: "Our best performances have always been when the crowds are behind us, which we had on Sunday."

# Pensioner Jailed for Historic Child Sex Abuse in Devon

A pensioner has been sentenced to two years in prison for historic sexual abuse that remained hidden for more than three decades.

Deryk Alex-Sanders, 81, of Denys Road, Totnes, pleaded guilty to three charges of indecent assault against an eight-year-old girl who visited his home. The offences only came to light when the victim disclosed the abuse during counselling sessions more than 30 years later.

At Exeter Crown Court, Judge Phillip Wassall condemned the lasting impact of the crimes. "The impact of assaults on young children when they are growing up can be buried in their subconscious for many years until something triggers the memory," he said.

The judge added: "You have had 30 years living a good and healthy life while the victim has spent that length of time trying to deal with the consequences of this offence."

The court heard that Alex-Sanders had a previous conviction for similar assaults on another girl around the same time, for which he received a nine-month suspended sentence in 1997.

Defence solicitor Martin Salloway told the court that Alex-Sanders is now in very poor health, which would make imprisonment particularly difficult. However, Judge Wassall determined that a custodial sentence was necessary given the severity of the offences.

# Major Indian Call Center Scam Targeting US Taxpayers Uncovered

Indian police have dismantled one of the country's largest fraud operations after raiding call centers in Thane that targeted US citizens with fake tax demands.

Officers say the suspects obtained lists of US tax defaulters and used threats to obtain their bank details. The scam is said to have netted more than $150,000 (£118,000) a day, making it one of the biggest frauds in India's history.

Thane police officials said they were contacting the FBI to ask for help. Some 70 of those detained were formally arrested, police said, with the rest released pending further inquiries. Nine people believed to have led the scam have been identified.

The scammers pretended to be members of the US Internal Revenue Service, and told victims they owed back taxes. In some cases, the victims were duped into buying gift vouchers from different companies and bullied into revealing voucher ID numbers, police said. The scammers then made purchases with the voucher numbers.

Police say those involved in the scam at the Indian end retained 70% of the earnings, with 30% going to their US collaborators.

Paramvir Singh, the police commissioner of Thane, told reporters that 851 hard disks, high-end servers, and other electronic equipment had been seized.

Mr Singh said overnight raids on Wednesday had lasted well into the morning, and involved more than 200 policemen who raided buildings in three locations in the city.

Thane police superintendent Mahesh Patil told BBC Hindi that the investigation could open up cases from other countries as well.

A US State Department official said they were following the situation closely to confirm any US citizen involvement.

# Judge Rules Manslaughter Case "Highly Exceptional" as Man Receives 18-Month Sentence After River Death

A County Londonderry man whose assault led to another man's death by drowning has been told his case is "highly exceptional" as he received an 18-month sentence for manslaughter.

Darren Joseph Casey, 26, from Claragh Hill Grange in Kilrea, admitted the manslaughter of Owen Gerard McKeown, 21, on 5 May 2012. The judge ruled that Mr McKeown's death "was the tragic result of his own decision to jump into the River Bann."

Casey was initially sentenced to 15 months, with an additional three-month suspended term added. He will serve half of his sentence in prison, with the remainder on parole, meaning he could be released in as little as one month.

The court heard that Mr McKeown died after jumping into the river, running "no doubt in fear of further assault" from Casey. However, in a dramatic turn of events revealed in December proceedings, Casey himself stripped off and jumped into the river in an apparent attempt to rescue Mr McKeown.

While prosecutors acknowledged that Casey did not intend Mr McKeown's death, his guilty plea to manslaughter meant he accepted responsibility for the fatal outcome of his unlawful assault.

## The Fatal Incident

The defence revealed that Mr McKeown had travelled to Kilrea from Ballymena with Casey to obtain steroid drugs, which both men used as part of their body-building regime. While climbing over a fence, Mr McKeown allegedly struck Casey first, prompting Casey to punch him to the ground and continue his attack.

A group of canoeists witnessed a fully-clothed man jump into the river, swim away from the bank, and then disappear under the water. Another man then stripped off his clothing and entered the water in what appeared to be a rescue attempt.

Unable to save Mr McKeown, Casey returned to the bank, dressed, and drove away from the scene. A post-mortem examination determined that drowning was the cause of death, with indications that Mr McKeown may have been under the influence of drugs.

## Remorse and Cooperation

The defence emphasized Casey's genuine remorse, noting that he later went to police with his father "to do the right thing." Casey was so distraught that he could not be properly interviewed initially and required hospital admission.

Two men who had travelled from Ballymena with Casey provided statements corroborating his version of events. The defence lawyer described the case as "tragic and unfortunate," highlighting that Casey had put his own life in danger during the rescue attempt.

# Scotland Unveils National Plan to Combat Child Sexual Exploitation

Scotland has launched a comprehensive national action plan to tackle child sexual exploitation with "ruthless determination," Education Secretary Mike Russell announced to parliament.

The initiative comes in response to growing concerns following the revelation that 1,400 children were systematically sexually exploited in Rotherham, South Yorkshire, between 1997 and 2013. The scandal prompted several children's charities to call for Scotland to develop its own strategic response to the issue.

**Public Awareness Campaign**

At the heart of the plan is a public awareness campaign designed to help identify and prevent child sexual exploitation. The strategy will include issuing guidance to night-time workers, including taxi drivers and hotel staff, to help them recognize potential cases of abuse.

"We need to have an awareness of it that means it can never be repeated," Mr Russell told parliament. "We need to prosecute those who are guilty so they can never reoffend and we need to place in permanence the truth about who was accountable so that others never fail again."

The action plan also aims to ensure a consistent approach across Scotland to support those working to combat the problem.

**Strengthening Child Protection**

Mr Russell said he would implement recommendations from a report by Jackie Brock, Chief Executive of Children in Scotland. Key workers involved in child protection will be brought together before the end of the year to clarify their responsibilities and improve coordination.

The Care Inspectorate watchdog in Scotland had previously warned agencies against complacency on the issue, prompting the government to take action.

**Scale of the Problem**

While Police Scotland has insisted that systematic sexual abuse on the scale of Rotherham is "absolutely not" happening in Scotland, authorities acknowledge significant challenges remain. Police reported a large number of child rapes and hundreds of convictions for child sexual exploitation in the last year.

Martin Crewe, director of children's charity Barnardo's, said: "We are certain that there is widespread child abuse, but what we don't know is the exact nature and prevalence of it." However, he added: "I don't think that the exact nature of Rotherham is happening in Scotland now."

The NSPCC highlighted in January a rise in sexual abuse cases in Scotland involving children under 13.

**Historic Abuse Inquiry**

Meanwhile, Mr Russell confirmed the government is still considering whether to hold a further inquiry into historic child sex abuse, with a decision expected by Christmas.

"Some dreadful things happened in Scotland over many years to children who deserved so much better from those in positions of trust," Mr Russell said. "We must never forget what took place."

Police Scotland, which is establishing a dedicated child abuse investigation unit, welcomed the government's national plan.

# Lincoln City Held to Goalless Draw at Maidstone United

Lincoln City's hopes of reaching the 100-point milestone were dashed as they were held to a frustrating 0-0 draw at Maidstone United, unable to break down the stubborn home defense led by goalkeeper Lee Worgan.

The Imps started brightly and nearly broke the deadlock in the 17th minute when a clever one-two between Adam Marriott and Jack Muldoon created an opening, but Marriott's shot struck the outside of the post. Maidstone's best first-half chance saw Ross Etheridge produce an excellent save to deny Alex Flisher.

Lincoln continued to press after the interval, coming agonizingly close six minutes into the second half. Sean Raggett met Billy Knott's free-kick, directing it toward Muldoon, whose effort cannoned off the crossbar.

The visitors threw everything forward in search of a winner, with Raggett going closest in the dying moments. His header from a corner with just two minutes remaining flashed inches wide of the post.

Both managers made tactical substitutions throughout the match, with Lincoln introducing Alex Simmons and Elliot Whitehouse, while Maidstone brought on Jack Richards, Jack Paxman, and Bobby-Joe Taylor. Despite their dominance, Lincoln were left to rue their missed opportunities as Maidstone's resolute defending and Worgan's goalkeeping earned a valuable point.

# Equality Watchdog Seeks Court Injunction Against Landlord Over Discriminatory Letting Policy

The Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) has applied for an injunction against controversial Kent landlord Fergus Wilson over his discriminatory letting criteria that bans tenants of Indian and Pakistani origin.

In his latest letting policy, Mr Wilson has also excluded zero-hour contract workers, single parents, "battered wives", and parents with children under 18 from renting his properties.

The landlord, long regarded as Britain's biggest buy-to-let investor with hundreds of properties across Kent, has defended his controversial policy on economic grounds, insisting his motivation is to avoid financial risk.

EHRC chief executive Rebecca Hilsenrath confirmed the organisation had applied for an injunction at Central London County Court. "We have asked the court if it agrees with us that Mr Wilson's lettings policy contains unlawful criteria and, if so, to issue an injunction," she said.

The EHRC last month demanded written assurance from Mr Wilson that he would not refuse tenancies based on race, colour, nationality or national origins. The commission has now announced it will launch a separate investigation into his policy targeting women.

Despite receiving online abuse that required police intervention, Mr Wilson has refused to back down. "Given that I have not had any Indian or Pakistani person apply for a house during the past five years, I am not sure what the EHRC seeks to achieve," he stated.

He added: "Like any business we are consistently fine-tuning to best advantage."

Mr Wilson has denied being racist, claiming he has previously rented to "non-white" people, including Gurkhas. However, he controversially stated: "It is not the colour of their skin, but the smell of the curry. The EHRC appears to be saying that the purchaser then must let the house to someone who does cook curry."

Advocacy group Hope Not Hate condemned the landlord's stance. "Mr Wilson needs to join the 21st century," a spokesperson said. "It's almost as if he has taken a tick box to offend every vulnerable group in Britain. We hope these legal proceedings will help him rapidly re-focus his outdated views."

# Kenyan Footballer Miheso Alleges Assault at South African Club

Kenyan international footballer Miheso has accused South African club Golden Arrows of assault, claiming the incident occurred on 14 January at the club's Durban offices.

The 24-year-old winger, who has earned 14 caps and scored five goals for Kenya, is demanding action against the club. He seeks a transfer ban or other sanctions against Golden Arrows, alongside $22,000 in unpaid wages.

# England Lock George Kruis Out for Weeks After Ankle Surgery

England's George Kruis will miss several weeks of action after undergoing minor ankle surgery, Saracens director of rugby Mark McCall has confirmed.

James Haskell, Anthony Watson, Jack Nowell, Luke Cowan-Dickie, Manu Tuilagi, and Jack Clifford are all unavailable, whilst uncapped flankers Mike Williams and Sam Jones have been ruled out with broken bones.

# Asian Markets Surge on Strong China Export Data and Oil Price Rally

Asian stock markets rallied strongly on Wednesday, driven by positive economic data from China and rising oil prices.

China's export figures exceeded expectations, with the world's second-largest economy reporting an 18.7% surge in yuan-denominated exports for March compared with the same period last year. FIFA President Gianni Infantino has raised concerns about the future format of men's football at the Olympics, suggesting the current structure may need reconsideration.

Brazil won the men's tournament for the first time at Rio 2016, beating Germany at the Maracana Stadium. However, while Infantino feels the women's game has developed due to its inclusion in the Olympics, he says problems remain to be solved with the men's competition.

# Dutch Football Analytics Firm Wins Champions League Innovation Competition

A Netherlands-based data analytics company has won a prestigious football innovation competition, earning its founder a trip to the Champions League final and access to Uefa's Swiss headquarters.

SciSports triumphed at the Hype Foundation event held at Cardiff University's business school, beating nine other start-ups in pitches to major sports and technology brands including Uefa, Adidas, Amazon, and Microsoft.

The firm specializes in using data analytics to assess the quality and potential of football players worldwide. These statistics are then utilized by clubs, managers, and players themselves to inform recruitment decisions and transfer negotiations.

Giels Brouwer, SciSports' chef de mission, said he was "honoured" to win the competition. He revealed the idea originated from an unlikely source—the popular computer game Football Manager.

"It's a game where you can be a virtual manager and I was really addicted to it," Brouwer explained. "When I was in college, I said to my room mate 'we should do this with real data' and that's what we did."

As his prize, Brouwer will attend Saturday's Champions League final and participate in a special workshop at Uefa headquarters in Switzerland.

The competition attracted approximately 800 applications from start-ups globally, according to Amir Raveh, chief executive of Hype Foundation. Other innovations showcased at the event included nano-technology embedded in shirts to measure players' blood pressure and training aids designed for both professional and grassroots team development.

Bernd Wahler, who led the judging panel and previously served as chief marketing officer for Adidas and president of German club VfB Stuttgart, praised the entries.

"The quality of the start-ups is outstanding," Wahler said. "We all want to maintain the beauty of the fascinating game and at the same time welcome meaningful and exciting innovations. That's what this event is all about—showing the world the future of football."

The Hype Foundation previously organized a similar event for the 2016 Rio Olympics.

# Police Hand Phone-Hacking Corporate Charges File to Prosecutors

The Metropolitan Police have submitted a file of evidence to the Crown Prosecution Service regarding potential corporate liability charges related to the News of the World phone-hacking scandal.

Detectives from Operation Weeting, the Met's phone-hacking investigation, handed over the file on 23 July, focusing on News UK, the company formerly known as News International that owned the defunct tabloid.

The CPS confirmed receipt of a "full file of evidence for consideration". However, the BBC's Daniel Sandford cautioned that submission does not guarantee charges will be filed, though it indicates they remain under active consideration.

News UK, which also publishes the Times and the Sun, rebranded from News International in 2013. The News of the World closed in July 2011 amid widespread outrage after revelations that journalists had hacked phones belonging to royals, celebrities, and crime victims.

# Woman Guilty of Sexual Assault Through Elaborate Deception

A 25-year-old woman has been found guilty of sexually assaulting another woman by pretending to be a man during an elaborate deception that lasted several months.

Gayle Newland, from Willaston, Cheshire, was convicted at Chester Crown Court on three counts of sexual assault after a four-day trial. She was cleared of two other similar charges but faces serious consequences when she is sentenced in November.

The court heard how Newland created a fictitious male persona called "Kye Fortune" on Facebook and developed an online relationship with her victim beginning in 2011. The women struck up what the victim believed to be a friendship with a man, speaking frequently on the phone over an extended period.

Newland told her victim that "Kye" was unable to meet in person due to injuries sustained in a car accident and treatment for a brain tumour. However, the pair eventually arranged to meet for sexual encounters at a hotel, with Newland insisting her victim wear a blindfold throughout, claiming "he" was embarrassed by scarring from the accidents.

The victim testified that she always believed she was meeting a man and complied with the unusual demand to remain blindfolded during their encounters. The pair went on to spend more than 100 hours together in hotels and at the victim's flat between February and June 2013, during which the sexual assaults took place.

Prosecutors alleged that Newland used a prosthetic penis during the encounters and disguised herself by strapping bandages to her chest and wearing a woollen hat and swimsuit to maintain the deception.

The elaborate fraud was finally exposed during their final meeting when the victim removed her blindfold and discovered Newland instead of the man she believed she had been seeing. "In hindsight I wish I had ripped that mask off sooner," the victim told the court.

During the trial, Newland denied the charges and claimed the pair had been engaging in consensual role play and fantasy. She insisted the other woman had known she was female and that both of them had been struggling with their sexuality. Newland denied using a blindfold or wearing disguises, though she did admit to creating the fake Facebook profile.

Following the guilty verdict, Newland became distressed in court, shouting "How can you send me down for something I have not done?" and repeatedly saying "I don't understand" through tears.

Judge Roger Dutton said Newland had "serious issues surrounding her personality" and warned she may face "serious consequences" at sentencing. He described it as a "difficult sentencing exercise" and thanked jurors for their careful consideration.

Detective Inspector Clare Coleman of Cheshire Constabulary emphasized the impact on the victim, stating: "This was a highly elaborate deception where Newland abused the trust that the victim had in her. She has been extremely upset by what has happened and there is no doubt there will be a lasting psychological impact on her."

Newland was released on bail pending sentencing.

# Horse Injured in Stable Fire Started by Burglars at Hampshire Farm

Emergency services responded to a devastating incident at a farm in Horris Hill, Newtown Common, early Wednesday morning after burglars targeted a tack store and set fire to a horse box.

The thieves made off with nine saddles valued at £12,000 and several bridles during the raid. However, the situation escalated when suspects set fire to a horse box truck, with flames quickly spreading to an adjacent stable building.

Although quick-thinking occupants managed to rescue horses trapped inside the burning stable, two animals sustained injuries. One horse suffered serious burns to its back and required treatment.

Stable owner Martin Pope expressed his anger at the incident: "They've caused an enormous amount of damage, threatened all the horses' lives and any humans who were trying to save the horses."

Det Con Alex Hall of Hampshire Constabulary stated the offence was "extremely rare" and that it appeared causing injury to the horses was not the offenders' intention. Nevertheless, he urged local horse owners to remain vigilant and report suspicious activity.

Police believe the incident occurred between 02:30 and 03:30 GMT Wednesday morning. Hampshire Constabulary is appealing for witnesses and anyone with information to come forward to assist with their investigation.

**Edwards Header Secures Dramatic Comeback Win for Partick Thistle at Hamilton**

Partick Thistle completed a remarkable turnaround at New Douglas Park, coming from behind to defeat Hamilton Academical 2-1 and boost their hopes of a top-six finish in the Scottish Premiership.

Greg Docherty had given the hosts an early lead with a powerful 12-yard strike that rattled into the roof of the net. The 19-year-old, who has been with Hamilton since he was nine years old, was developing quite a habit of scoring against the Jags – this was his third career goal, and the second time Partick had fallen victim to his clinical finishing.

Docherty's opener owed much to the excellent work of Gramoz Kurtaj down the left flank. The German forward held up the ball intelligently before rolling it diagonally towards the penalty spot, where Docherty converted emphatically, his shot taking a slight deflection on its way past the goalkeeper.

Hamilton could have doubled their advantage before half-time when Eamonn Brophy, deputising for suspended Carlton Morris, collected Docherty's pass and finished into the far corner, only to see his effort ruled out for offside.

The visitors struggled initially after losing Liam Lindsay to a warm-up injury, with Australian defender Ryan Edwards drafted in as a late replacement. However, Partick made the perfect start to the second period when Mathias Pogba drew them level.

The Frenchman, brother of Juventus and France star Paul Pogba, was in the right place at the right time at the back post to neatly nod home a measured delivery from Steven Lawless. It was a well-executed downward header that gave Michael McGovern no chance in the Hamilton goal.

Brophy remained a threat for the home side, with one angled effort flashing narrowly over the crossbar as Hamilton pressed for a winner. However, it was Partick who had the final say.

Late in the match, substitute Kris Doolan provided the decisive moment, delivering a pinpoint cross that found Edwards making a positive run into the box. The Australian, who hadn't even expected to start, powered home a header for his first goal in Jags colours to complete a memorable afternoon.

The victory lifts Partick Thistle above Dundee into seventh place and will surely have their supporters dreaming of a late surge into the top six rather than worrying about any relegation concerns.

For Hamilton, it was another frustrating afternoon at home, as player-manager Martin Canning watched his side fail to capitalise on Kilmarnock's earlier defeat to Celtic, leaving relegation worries very much alive.

# Killer of EastEnders Actress Has Whole-Life Sentence Upheld by Appeal Court

Arthur Simpson-Kent, 49, has lost his appeal against the whole-life prison sentence imposed for the murders of his partner, former EastEnders actress Syan Blake, and their two young sons.

Simpson-Kent stabbed Ms Blake to death along with their sons Zachary, eight, and Amon, four. He killed them when he learnt Ms Blake was planning to leave him and take their sons away, the court heard. Judges upheld a decision that he should receive the most "severe punishment for his horrific crimes" on Tuesday.

Following the murder in December 2015, Simpson-Kent painted over the bloodstains in the family bungalow in Erith, south-east London, before fleeing to his native Ghana in January. He was arrested at Heathrow Airport in February after being extradited and admitted murdering his family in June.

He was sentenced at the Old Bailey last October by a judge who said he had been left in "no doubt" he should receive the most severe punishment available for his "truly horrific" crimes.

Lord Thomas, describing the murders of the three vulnerable victims as horrific and involving "extreme brutality", said the court was "entirely satisfied" that the sentencing judge was entitled to reach the conclusion that it was a case where "just punishment" required the imposition of a whole-life order.

The appeal judges rejected argument on the killer's behalf that a "very long finite" sentence in the region of 40 years would have been sufficient - and would have given him some hope of release once served.

In throwing out Simpson-Kent's challenge, Lord Thomas said that for a whole-life sentence to be imposed the offending must be "exceptionally high". He said: "We have to look at the whole of the circumstances and to consider whether this was a case where the seriousness of the offending was exceptionally high - we have no doubt that it was."

Ms Blake played Frankie Pierre in 56 episodes of EastEnders between 1996 and 1997. She went on to work as a voice-over artist and sign language interpreter.

# Robbie Coltrane Drama Films in Hull City Centre

Filming for a new Channel 4 drama starring Robbie Coltrane and Julie Walters has brought disruption to Hull city centre today.

Scenes for the four-part series "National Treasure" are being shot on Lowgate, with the historic Three John Scotts pub doubling as London's famous Old Bailey courthouse.

The production has necessitated road closures from 10:00 GMT until 17:00, with diversions directing traffic via Silver Street and High Street.

The drama explores the impact of historical sexual offence allegations against a celebrity figure. The Old Bailey, formally known as the Central Criminal Court of England and Wales, typically handles the capital's most serious criminal cases.

# Turkish Prosecutor Dies After Hostage Crisis at Istanbul Courthouse

A Turkish prosecutor has died from injuries sustained during a dramatic hostage situation at an Istanbul courthouse that ended in a violent confrontation between police and armed gunmen.

Mehmet Selim Kiraz was taken hostage on Tuesday by suspected members of a banned Marxist revolutionary group at the Caglayan courthouse. The prosecutor had been leading an investigation into the death of Berkin Elvan, a teenager who died after being struck by a police tear gas canister during anti-government protests in 2013.

The hostage takers, believed to be affiliated with the Revolutionary People's Liberation Party-Front (DHKP-C), released disturbing images showing a gun held to Mr Kiraz's head during the six-hour standoff on the courthouse's sixth floor.

According to Istanbul's police chief Selami Altunok, authorities attempted negotiations with the gunmen for six hours before deciding to storm the prosecutor's office after hearing gunshots from inside. The operation resulted in the deaths of both gunmen, while Mr Kiraz was critically wounded and later succumbed to his injuries.

The hostage takers had issued demands through an online statement, threatening to kill the prosecutor if their conditions were not met. Sukriye Erden, a lawyer who participated in negotiations, revealed that the gunmen wanted police to publicly name four security service members allegedly connected to Berkin Elvan's death.

Elvan was just 14 years old when he was struck in the head by a tear gas canister in June 2013 while going to buy bread during mass demonstrations that swept across Turkey. He remained in a coma for nine months before dying in an Istanbul hospital in 2014.

The teenager's death became a flashpoint in Turkish politics when President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who was prime minister at the time, controversially claimed the boy had been carrying a slingshot and was involved with "terrorist organisations."

The Turkish government imposed a ban on live television coverage of the incident, citing security concerns. The DHKP-C is designated as a terrorist organization by Turkey, the European Union, and the United States. The group previously claimed responsibility for a suicide bombing at the US embassy in Ankara in February 2013 that killed a security guard.

# Derby County Boss Gary Rowett Vows to Focus on Football After CEO Sam Rush Dismissal

Derby County manager Gary Rowett has insisted the shock departure of chief executive Sam Rush will not affect his team's preparations for next season.

The Championship club removed Rush from his role as chief executive on Wednesday, citing "gross misconduct" and a "breach of fiduciary duty" as the reason for his departure.

Rush, who joined in 2013 and signed a new five-year deal in October 2015, has said the matter is with his lawyers.

Rowett told BBC Radio Derby the news would not impact on the football side.

"That is my only real concern and that is going to be unaffected, so we move forward," he added.

"In terms of the way I have worked, in the last five or six years, I've tended to have a big hand in transfers and a lot of the work behind the scenes.

"That adds extra workload but I've quite enjoyed that, because it means it's the squad I've wanted to build and I can feel responsible for the results.

"This summer, certainly, that's going to be very similar to how we have done it before. Whatever has happened has happened. That is nothing to do with me."

Rowett, who has only been in charge at the Championship club since March, said chairman Mel Morris' decision to sack Rush was not his focus.

"The club obviously took the course of action that they felt necessary for the benefit of the club," the former Birmingham boss added.

**Owen Bradley, BBC Radio Derby Sport**

It's a huge surprise. Sam Rush was named Football League chief executive of the year in 2014 and has been a massive part of the club since he arrived.
