Police Scotland is once again delighted to work with our key partners to ensure that people gain maximum enjoyment from the city over the next few weeks and remain safe in doing so."

# Sir Tom Jones Thanks Fans for Support After Wife's Death

Sir Tom Jones has expressed his gratitude to fans for their messages of support following the death of his wife, Lady Melinda Rose Woodward, known as Linda, who passed away earlier this month after battling cancer.

The couple, who hailed from Pontypridd in Rhondda Cynon Taff, shared 59 years of marriage. In a statement posted on his website under the heading "A little note from Tom," the legendary singer wrote: "So many beautiful and meaningful things were said and reading these genuine and lovely messages has lifted us all."

Sir Tom and Linda's love story began when they were just 15 years old, meeting at a phone box at the end of his street in Treforest. They married at age 16 in 1957 and later had that very phone box relocated to their Los Angeles home as a sentimental keepsake. The couple had one son, Mark, who now serves as Sir Tom's manager.

Lady Woodward died at Cedars Sinai Hospital in Los Angeles on 10 April. The singer cancelled several concerts when his wife fell ill.

In his message, Sir Tom thanked fans for their "heartfelt" notes of sympathy and support, adding "See you soon."

According to his website, the singer who achieved his first number one hit with "It's Not Unusual" in 1965, is scheduled to return to performing at the Hampton Court Palace Festival in London on 8 June, followed by concerts throughout the UK, Norway and Spain.

Two Welsh health boards are to receive £68.4m in emergency funding from the Welsh Government to address budget shortfalls.

Betsi Cadwaladr in north Wales and Hywel Dda in west Wales are both projected to exceed their budgets for 2016-17. The money will be drawn from Welsh Government reserves.

Health boards now operate on three-year budget cycles following criticism of repeated financial bail-outs. Last year, Hywel Dda overspent by £31.2m whilst Betsi Cadwaladr exceeded its budget by £19.5m, highlighting ongoing financial pressures within Welsh healthcare services.

# Eden Hazard Completes Chelsea Move After Choosing Blues Over Manchester United

The Belgium international, 21, has agreed personal terms and passed a medical with the Blues.

Eden Hazard's journey to Stamford Bridge represents one of the summer's most sought-after transfers, with the talented winger ultimately choosing Chelsea's "project" over rival suitors.

Born in La Louviere, Belgium in January 1991, Hazard has enjoyed a meteoric rise through European football. He made his first-team debut for Lille in November 2007 in a 2-0 defeat by Nancy, and within a year had earned his first Belgium cap against Luxembourg at just 18 years old.

In September 2008, Hazard became Lille's youngest-ever goalscorer with a strike against Auxerre in a 3-2 victory. His precocious talent was further recognized when he won the Young Player of the Year award twice, in May 2010 becoming the first player to achieve this feat.

The 2010-11 season proved particularly successful as Hazard helped Lille secure a league and cup double whilst claiming Player of the Year honors. He notched his first international goal for Belgium in October 2011 and won Player of the Year again in May 2012 after netting 17 league goals.

"When they won the Champions League I told myself, 'Why not Chelsea?'," said Hazard. "There was a struggle between Chelsea and [Manchester] United but, for me, Chelsea has the best project. It's a wonderful club."

Chelsea are reportedly paying £32m for the youngster, who added: "The team is young and I have a better chance to play there. If I play well enough at Chelsea, I could win my place in the starting team."

In his final season at Lille, Hazard scored 21 goals in 48 games, signing off with a hat-trick against Nancy last month. He joins Germany international Marko Marin as Chelsea's second major addition since January.

# Cricket Commentator's Tip to Captain Under Investigation by Cricket Australia

Cricket Australia has launched an investigation after a television commentator appeared to influence a captain's bowling decision during a Big Bash League match between Adelaide Strikers and Sydney Thunder.

Adelaide Strikers captain Brad Hodge was told by Network Ten commentator Mark Howard that bowler Ben Laughlin had dismissed Sydney Thunder batsman Shane Watson twice in eight balls previously. Hodge, who was wearing a microphone and earpiece to communicate with the broadcast team between overs, responded by bringing Laughlin into the attack.

During the exchange, Howard told Hodge: "Our master statistician Lawrie Colliver tells us that Laughlin has got Watson twice in the last eight balls he's bowled him in this competition."

Hodge replied: "Really? I'll bring him on next over then. Let's get him into the game."

The incident prompted former England batsman Kevin Pietersen, who was co-commentating but not involved in the exchange, to comment: "Very naughty. Very, very naughty, Howie."

Cricket Australia issued a statement saying its integrity unit is investigating "to ensure the comments made during the broadcast did not jeopardise the integrity of last night's match." Network Ten subsequently apologised for Howard's remarks.

Although Laughlin did not dismiss Watson, the Thunder batsman eventually scored 39 from 26 balls before being caught by Laughlin off Jake Lehmann's bowling. Thunder were dismissed for 101 chasing 178, leaving them bottom of the eight-team table and eliminated from knockout stage contention.

# Massive Iceberg Breaks Away From Greenland's Jakobshavn Glacier

A colossal section of ice measuring 12.4 square kilometres has broken away from Greenland's Jakobshavn Glacier in what scientists describe as one of the largest calving events ever recorded at this location.

Satellite imagery from the European Space Agency indicates the dramatic break-up occurred between 13 and 19 August, pushing the glacier's calving front back several kilometres.

Jakobshavn serves as a major drainage channel for the Greenland ice sheet, responsible for producing approximately 10% of all its icebergs. Once detached, these massive ice formations travel through a lengthy fjord before entering the Davis Strait and eventually making their way towards the Atlantic Ocean. The glacier holds historical significance, as it is widely believed to be the source of the iceberg that tragically sank the Titanic.

Scientists have observed that Jakobshavn moves at tens of metres per day during summer months, establishing it as one of Greenland's fastest-flowing ice streams.

The European Space Agency has been monitoring the situation using EU Sentinel satellites. The Sentinel-1a radar platform can penetrate cloud cover and map flow and elevation changes, whilst the Sentinel-2a optical spacecraft provides contextual imagery.

According to ESA calculations, assuming the ice depth of approximately 1,400 metres, the calved volume would equal roughly 17.5 cubic kilometres—enough ice to blanket Manhattan Island with a layer 300 metres thick.

Whilst substantial for Greenland, this calving event remains relatively modest compared to Antarctic ice sheet break-ups, where tabular bergs spanning thousands of square kilometres can separate from the southern polar region.

# Temple Circus Roundabout to Be Replaced with Public Square

Bristol's Temple Circus roundabout near Temple Meads station is set to be transformed into a public square with improved city access routes.

A Bristol City Council spokesman said the new square would "give life to the area day and night."

The redevelopment is part of a wider £21m investment in the Temple Quarter Enterprise Zone.

Public consultation on the proposals will run until 18 February 2015, with an exhibition of the plans displayed at the Engine Shed from Tuesday, 13 January through Friday, 30 January.

The council hopes the transformation will create a more vibrant and accessible gateway to the city centre.

# Tall Ships Set Sail from Belfast as Thousands Line Coast

Belfast served as the starting point for the prestigious Tall Ships Races, which commenced off the County Antrim coast on Monday. The magnificent fleet made its way towards Bangor in County Down before completing the ceremonial departure at Whitehead in County Antrim.

Spectators were treated to a thrilling pre-race performance by the Red Arrows aerobatic display team before the vessels departed. The event showcased an impressive 50 ships representing 15 different nations.

Police estimated that up to 300,000 people gathered along the Antrim and north Down coastlines to witness the spectacular send-off. This marked Belfast's second time hosting the event, having previously welcomed the Tall Ships in 2009.

The official race began five miles off Portrush, County Antrim, at 10:00 BST on Monday. Following their departure from Northern Ireland, the international fleet will visit six ports across five countries, including stops in Aalesund and Kristiansand in Norway, before concluding in Aalborg, Denmark.

# Brighton Refuse Workers Suspend Strike as Talks Continue

A planned strike by refuse and recycling truck drivers in Brighton and Hove scheduled for Tuesday has been suspended, though industrial action remains scheduled for 3 October, the GMB union has confirmed.

The drivers, who walked out earlier this month, are in dispute with the council over pay, staff grading and responsibility issues. The GMB union said a work-to-rule policy would continue during the negotiations.

The union claims that some council employees are performing equivalent work to their members whilst receiving higher pay. GMB also alleges the authority has failed to "consult meaningfully" over new working practices and ongoing concerns about round allocation and distribution.

GMB representative Mark Turner indicated further talks with the council are planned for next Tuesday.

Brighton and Hove City Council welcomed the suspension of strike action and stated it is examining a "full service redesign to ensure we meet the needs of the city and to resolve work-to-rule".

In a statement, the council said: "We cannot favour one group of workers over another and increasing allowances for one group of staff would require us to increase it for many others at great cost to the council's overall pay bill."

The council noted that an agreement reached with trade unions last year aimed to ensure equal pay compliance.

Last summer, similar industrial action resulted in waste accumulating on city streets.

# Tiny Tail Cameras Reveal Secret Lives of Tool-Making New Caledonian Crows

Ecologists have fitted wild New Caledonian crows with specially designed miniature tail cameras to observe their behavior beneath their bellies, capturing rare footage of these remarkable birds crafting and using sophisticated tools in their natural habitat.

The groundbreaking study, led by Christian Rutz from the University of St Andrews in the UK, aimed to understand why New Caledonian crows are among the rare bird species that use tools while most others don't. "I think the answer lies in figuring out how important tool use is in their everyday lives," Dr Rutz explained.

The research team analyzed nearly 12 hours of "crow cam" footage from 10 different birds, revealing surprising insights about their daily activities. Contrary to expectations, the crows spent remarkably little time making or using tools—only about 3% of their total observation time. Only four of the 10 birds even picked up a tool during the recording period.

Instead, the crows dedicated most of their time to foraging for food using their beaks, particularly tearing strips from paperbark trees in search of grubs. Their sturdy beaks proved perfectly adequate for this task. "But every now and then, they suddenly switch to tool use - in the very same trees," Dr Rutz noted. "We don't understand what is happening there."

Despite the limited tool use, the team captured extraordinary footage of two different crows not merely using sticks but actually manufacturing hooks—a sophisticated tool-making behavior. The birds snap off one branch from a forked twig, leaving a small portion of the main stem attached to create a hooked tool.

"When we got that footage it was a proper high-five moment in the field camp," Dr Rutz said enthusiastically. While laboratory experiments and binocular observations had previously documented this hook-making behavior, this marked the first time researchers obtained video evidence of it occurring unprompted in the wild.

Jolyon Troscianko from the University of Exeter emphasized the challenges of studying these birds: "New Caledonian crows are notoriously difficult to observe, not just because of the challenging terrain of their tropical habitats, but also because they can be quite sensitive to disturbance."

The research team employed newly designed cameras that stored footage on micro SD cards rather than transmitting signals, eliminating the need for researchers to trek through difficult forest terrain with antennas. The devices record for approximately one week before automatically falling off the birds, and researchers locate them using tiny radio beacons.

"We got much longer, uninterrupted video recordings," Dr Rutz said, highlighting how the improved technology has advanced their understanding of these intelligent birds.

# Man Bailed in Murder Investigation of Wisbech Widow

A 58-year-old man arrested on suspicion of murder has been released on bail following the death of Una Crown in Wisbech.

The widow was discovered in her Magazine Lane home on 13 January, having been stabbed and her body burned.

Mrs Crown was last seen alive on the morning of 11 January but had spoken to a friend by telephone on 12 January afternoon.

The man, arrested in Wisbech earlier this week, has been released pending further inquiries as police continue their investigation into the circumstances surrounding her death.

# UN Chief Ban Ki-moon Hints at South Korean Presidential Bid

UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon has strongly hinted he may run for South Korea's presidency, as political turmoil engulfs the country following the impeachment of President Park Geun-hye.

Mr Ban's term as the world's top diplomat expires at the end of December. In his final press conference as UN chief, Mr Ban said that after some rest he will return to South Korea and consider how best to help his country.

South Korea's next presidential election is scheduled to be held in December 2017. However, a poll could take place within two months after the country's parliament voted to impeach current President Park Geun-hye over an influence-peddling scandal.

Ms Park is accused of allowing a close friend to profit from her connections with the presidency. If the country's constitutional court upholds last week's impeachment vote, she will become the first sitting South Korean president to be deposed in the country's democratic era - and a new presidential election will be held within 60 days. The constitutional court has 180 days to make a final ruling.

Mr Ban's comments come amid ongoing protests in the South Korean capital, Seoul. Large crowds are expected to gather this weekend to demand that Ms Park resigns immediately, and to urge the constitutional court to formally remove her from office.

This will be the eighth consecutive week of protests against Ms Park. While the rallies have been largely peaceful, there are fears that demonstrators could clash with thousands of the president's supporters who have planned their own protest near the court.

Ms Park's lawyer, Lee Joong-hwan, has said the court should restore the president's powers because there is insufficient evidence to justify her removal.

The case against Ms Park rests on her relationship with long-time friend Choi Soon-sil, who faces charges of coercion and abuse of power. It is alleged that after Ms Park became president in 2013, Ms Choi, 60, used their friendship to pressure powerful corporations into donating to foundations she controlled and then siphoned off funds for her personal use.

Prosecutors say Ms Park had a "considerable" role in the alleged corruption. The president has denied that, but apologised for putting her trust in her jailed friend. Ms Choi's criminal trial will begin on 20 December.

# Thieves Steal £550,000 Worth of Statues in Targeted Raid

Three valuable statues worth approximately £550,000 have been stolen from a property in South Gloucestershire during a targeted break-in.

The theft occurred at Bath Road, Cold Ashton, between 7 and 9 May. The most valuable item taken was a wishing well statue worth £500,000, along with two other statues depicting a horse and rider, each valued at around £25,000.

Avon and Somerset Police described the raid as "targeted" and "well-planned". PC Simon McFall said the operation would have required multiple people due to the statues' significant weight and size.

"It is more than likely that a van or other large vehicle was used to transport them," he added.

Police are appealing for witnesses and anyone with information to contact the force.

# Kobe Bryant Launches Investment Fund with Tech Entrepreneur Jeff Stibel

Retired basketball legend Kobe Bryant has partnered with technology entrepreneur Jeff Stibel to launch a formal investment fund focused on technology, media, and data companies.

Mr Bryant, the former captain of the Los Angeles Lakers, told the Wall Street Journal he felt he has a talent for identifying entrepreneurs. It is that talent and not his star power that the pair say they hope to bring to the companies they invest in.

The "Bryant Stibel" fund will invest in tech, media and data companies. Mr Stibel is an entrepreneur and investor who founded several companies including Web.com.

Mr Bryant, 37, retired from basketball earlier this year after a 20-year career. He has invested with Mr Stibel before, but this fund is the first formal partnership between them. The pair are financing the fund themselves.

Since 2013, they have invested in 15 companies together including sports website The Players Tribune, videogame designer Scopely, and legal-services company LegalZoom.

Mr Bryant who was known for his strong work ethic in basketball said, similar skills are needed for sport and growing a business. "It's the inner belief that a person has that he will endure no matter what the obstacle may be. It's that persistence, the entrepreneur doing what he or she truly believes in and truly loves to do," he said.

The pair said the fund will last a few years and look to target companies where they feel they can add value through their business insight, and not through Mr Bryant's celebrity.

Mr Stibel told the Wall Street Journal, "We don't want to be in the business of investing in companies so someone can use Kobe as an endorser. That's not interesting. The point is to add real value".

Mr Bryant is not the first athlete to enter the investment world. An increasing number of sports starts and retired athletes are investing in venture capital funds and start-ups. Former basketball player Shaquille O'Neal has invested in several tech start-ups. Footballers David Beckham and Thierry Henry have both turned their attentions to investing since retiring.

# Wakefield Trinity's Adam Walker Dropped from Scotland World Cup Squad After Positive Cocaine Test

Wakefield Trinity forward Adam Walker has been removed from Scotland's Rugby League World Cup squad after testing positive for cocaine.

The 26-year-old prop failed a drugs test following his team's Super League match at Widnes on 14 July. Both Wakefield Trinity and the Rugby Football League immediately suspended Walker pending further investigation.

Scotland Rugby League chairman Keith Hogg announced the decision, stating: "We totally support the RFL anti-doping regulations and the action undertaken by Wakefield Trinity. We will be withdrawing Adam Walker from our extended World Cup squad."

Scotland head coach Steve McCormack has moved quickly to replace Walker by adding two promising players to his 37-man squad for the World Cup in Australia later this year. New Zealand Warriors' James Bell and South Sydney Rabbitohs' Campbell Graham have been called up after both made their National Rugby League debuts last week.

McCormack expressed his enthusiasm about the new additions: "We've known about them since last year and have been really pleased to see the progress that James and Campbell have been making. It was great to see them make their NRL debuts within a few days of each other."

# Thousands join social media tribute to teenage rider Olivia Inglis

The #rideforolivia tribute was launched following the death of Australian Olivia Inglis, 17, in a fall on Sunday. Hundreds of thousands of social media users from dozens of countries have been posting and sharing photos of their own horses using the hashtag.

Olympic gold medallist Charlotte Dujardin is among the high-profile figures to have joined in the tributes. Fellow British dressage rider and gold medallist Carl Hester has also paid tribute.

The movement echoes a similar social campaign to mark the death of Australian cricketer Phillip Hughes in 2014. The hashtags #putoutyourbats and #putyourbatsout were tweeted and shared across platforms such as Instagram and Facebook along with photos of cricket bats.

As of 08:00 GMT on Thursday, more than 120,000 people had posted photographs and videos for #rideforolivia on Instagram alone. The images will be used to create a mosaic of Olivia for her family, following a call from the bloodstock company which her family runs.

"We have been overwhelmed by the kindness and sympathy from family and friends throughout the school, equestrian and thoroughbred communities," parents Arthur and Charlotte said in a family statement.

The global outpouring of support demonstrates the tight-knit nature of the international equestrian community and the profound impact of Olivia's tragic passing.

# Man Admits Life-Threatening Assault on Islay After Pub Altercation

A man has admitted assaulting another man to the danger of his life following a violent attack outside a pub on the Isle of Islay.

Andrew MacGillivray, 33, punched Keith Cameron and stood on his chest, causing his ribs to crack, near the Ardview Inn in Port Ellen on 23 March last year. He pleaded guilty to assaulting the 41-year-old to the danger of his life at the High Court in Glasgow, where judges heard Mr Cameron was fortunate to be alive.

The court was told that MacGillivray became involved in an argument with a woman inside the bar. Mr Cameron, known locally as "Cabana," attempted to intervene and calm the situation. MacGillivray was subsequently asked to leave the premises but waited outside for his victim to emerge.

When Mr Cameron left the pub, MacGillivray knocked him to the ground with a single punch before launching a sustained attack on him as he lay defenceless. He then stood on Mr Cameron's ribs with such force that they cracked audibly.

The severity of the injuries was such that when a passing couple who knew Mr Cameron discovered him, they were unable to recognise him due to the extent of his facial injuries.

MacGillivray, a father-of-three, returned home and told his wife: "I think I've killed Cabana. I hope he's OK. I know I hurt his ribs." He later told police that he heard the ribs crack and that Mr Cameron's chest "went as flat as his stomach."

Before his arrest, MacGillivray told his father-in-law: "I did it - I would do it again and worse. If you want to be hard, you have to act hard."

Mr Cameron suffered facial injuries, damage to his eye, and significant chest fractures. He required treatment at the Southern General Hospital in Glasgow after being airlifted from Islay.

Medical experts told the court that the chest injuries were more commonly associated with heavy objects falling on people and that Mr Cameron's life had been in danger.

Sentence on MacGillivray was deferred.

# Mother 'Staged Baby's Death on London Bus', Court Hears

A mother accused of murdering her 16-week-old daughter "staged" the infant's death on a London bus after the baby was already dead, a court has heard.

Rosalin Baker, 25, and her partner Jeffrey Wiltshire, 52, deny murdering baby Imani and attempting to cover up her death by making it appear she died in public.

The Old Bailey was told that Imani was already deceased when Ms Baker boarded the number 25 bus in Stratford, east London, with her daughter's body.

Passenger Fjoralba Shmitz told jurors how Ms Baker gestured to her while on the phone, saying: "There's something wrong with my baby."

Ms Shmitz described the harrowing scene: "I saw the baby's face. I touched her left cheek. It was cold. The baby was not breathing. I tried to help but I didn't manage to do so."

The witness said she took the child and asked the bus driver to call emergency services. "I became distressed because the baby was not moving," she told the court. "I thought that the baby was dead."

She described how she returned to the bus seat with the infant, where another passenger, believed to be Spanish, "started praying."

When asked about Ms Baker's reaction, Ms Shmitz said the mother was notably calm. "She was not crying, she was not shouting, she was not speaking," the witness testified.

Under cross-examination by Icah Peart QC, Ms Shmitz confirmed Ms Baker appeared "very relaxed" and seemed detached during the "distressing episode."

Jurors have previously heard that Imani had suffered multiple attacks before her death, sustaining 40 rib fractures, a fractured wrist, and head injuries.

Both Ms Baker and Mr Wiltshire, from Newham, east London, deny charges of murder and causing or allowing the death of a child.

The trial continues.

# Mad Men Star Jon Hamm Completes Rehabilitation Treatment

Jon Hamm, the acclaimed actor best known for portraying the complex Don Draper in AMC's hit series Mad Men, has completed treatment for alcohol addiction at a rehabilitation facility, his representatives have confirmed.

The actor, who has asked for "privacy and sensitivity" following the revelation, sought help with the support of his long-time partner, actress and film-maker Jennifer Westfeldt. The timing of his treatment comes as Hamm has been actively promoting the final season of the Emmy-winning drama series.

According to celebrity website TMZ, which broke the story, the Golden Globe-winning actor underwent a 30-day treatment program at Silver Hill Hospital in New Canaan, Connecticut, a facility known for treating high-profile clients.

Throughout Mad Men's eight-year run, Hamm has frequently been asked about similarities between himself and his hard-drinking character. In a 2012 interview with the Daily Mail, he noted, "I don't drink as much as Don Draper. I would be unconscious if I did."

However, the actor has previously been candid about his struggles with alcohol, particularly following his father's death from diabetes complications in 1991. Hamm, who lost his mother a decade earlier, found himself orphaned at age 20.

"It just changed everything," he told GQ magazine last year. "It was just a profound sense of being alone. I was at a crossroads. It really could have gone the wrong way."

Despite the personal challenges, Hamm's career continues to flourish. Beyond Mad Men's conclusion, he has secured roles in two Netflix series: Tina Fey's critically-acclaimed Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt and the upcoming Wet Hot American Summer prequel series.

The actor has also built an impressive film resume, appearing in The Town, Bridesmaids, and Kissing Jessica Stein, where he first met Westfeldt.

Representatives for Hamm have requested that his privacy be respected during this time.

# Cardiff Blues Reject WRU Takeover Option to Focus on Arms Park Redevelopment

Cardiff Blues have unanimously decided not to pursue the option of a Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) takeover, the region's chief executive Richard Holland has confirmed.

The announcement comes as the Blues continue negotiations with Cardiff Athletic Club over extending their lease at Cardiff Arms Park, which is set to expire in January 2022.

In an open letter to supporters, Holland revealed that "amicable discussions" had taken place regarding potential WRU assistance during the possible redevelopment of the historic stadium. However, the region's board has chosen to maintain independence while exploring alternative paths forward.

"We will continue to explore the best way forward for the future of our region," Holland stated.

The decision follows earlier comments from WRU chief executive Martyn Phillips in May, when he described talks over a potential Blues takeover as "embryonic." The announcement also comes shortly after a vote that enabled the WRU to take over Blues' regional rivals, Newport Gwent Dragons.

## Lease Negotiations Progress

The Blues' stadium redevelopment plans hinge on securing a new agreement with Cardiff Athletic Club (CAC), the body comprising Cardiff's tennis, bowls, hockey and cricket clubs that maintains a clubhouse at the Arms Park.

A CAC spokesperson confirmed that negotiations are continuing, saying: "I can confirm that negotiations are ongoing and we hope to call an EGM [extraordinary general meeting] in the not too distant future."

However, the spokesperson added that practical considerations, including the Champions League Final on 3 June, would likely delay any meeting for several weeks.

## Redevelopment Vision

Holland emphasized the urgency of securing the Blues' long-term future at their traditional home, noting that only five years remain on the current lease while annual maintenance costs continue to rise.

"The history and heritage of Cardiff Rugby at Cardiff Arms Park is of paramount importance to the board and it is essential to protect all elements of this great club and its iconic home," he said.

The Blues are seeking a new 150-year lease with development rights from CAC. Holland expressed optimism about reaching an agreement with the CAC management board.

Previously announced plans envision transforming the Arms Park into a modern 15,000-capacity stadium featuring a retractable pitch and sliding roof, enabling the venue to host concerts as well as rugby matches. Additional proposals include an exhibition centre, hotel and residential flats.

Holland indicated he would soon present "concept ideas" for the redevelopment, ranging from replacing the North and South stands to a complete site redevelopment, while maintaining rugby as the priority use.

"These concepts are purely an indication of what could be achieved," he explained.

# Syrian Refugees Cast Votes in Presidential Election at Embassies in Beirut and Amman

Polling stations at Syrian embassies in Beirut and Amman opened Wednesday for expatriate voting ahead of Syria's controversial presidential election, drawing massive crowds of Syrian refugees eager to cast their ballots.

The voting comes as the United Nations reports that 2.8 million Syrian refugees have fled to neighbouring countries since the conflict began. President Bashar al-Assad is widely expected to secure a third seven-year term in the June 3 election, which Western nations have dismissed as a sham.

## Massive Turnout in Beirut

Thousands of Syrians flocked to their embassy in the hills overlooking Beirut, creating unprecedented scenes. BBC correspondent Jim Muir, reporting from the scene, described the massive turnout as producing "scenes rarely observed at any embassy or polling station in the world."

The event transformed at times into what appeared to be a rowdy support rally for President Assad, abandoning typical election decorum. As the only polling station available for all of Lebanon, where an estimated 1.5 million or more Syrians currently reside, the embassy was completely overwhelmed.

The voting congestion brought much of Beirut to a standstill, demonstrating to many Lebanese residents how deeply the Syrian crisis has penetrated their country. Of the one million Syrian refugees registered in Lebanon, approximately half are believed to be of voting age. Embassy officials indicated they may extend voting hours if large numbers are unable to participate.

## Regional Diplomatic Tensions

In Jordan's capital, Amman, voting proceeded just days after the kingdom expelled Syrian ambassador Bahjat Suleiman over what it termed "repeated insults" against the country.

According to Syria's state-run Sana news agency, voting also commenced at embassies in Russia, Malaysia, Sudan, and several other countries. However, the agency reported that the United Arab Emirates banned Syrians from voting, following similar prohibitions by France, Germany, and Belgium. Many expatriates living in countries where Syrian embassies closed in 2011 remain unable to vote.

## Controversial Election

The strength and assertiveness of the vote may reflect an underlying sentiment among many Syrians abroad that momentum favours the regime, observers suggest. The opposition coalition welcomed recent promises from President Obama for increased aid, though questions remain about whether such support can shift the balance given Western concerns about jihadi presence in rebel-controlled areas.

This marks the first time in decades that Syria has held a presidential election featuring multiple candidates. However, the two challengers remain largely unknown and have been unable to campaign equally with the president. Previous presidential terms were determined through referendums with only Assad family members on the ballot.

More than 160,000 people have died since the uprising against President Assad began in March 2011.

# Australian Government Website Accidentally Exposes Politicians' Phone Numbers

The mobile phone numbers of several former Australian prime ministers and hundreds of other politicians were inadvertently exposed on a government website for more than three months, Fairfax Media has reported.

The security breach affected Opposition Leader Bill Shorten and former prime ministers Julia Gillard, John Howard, and Paul Keating. Current Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull and some senior government members were not impacted by the incident.

The sensitive information was discovered on the Department of Parliamentary Services (DPS) website, where phone numbers appeared invisible but could be revealed when highlighted with a cursor or copied and pasted into another document.

In a statement to the BBC, the DPS explained that the numbers were included in a report detailing parliamentary phone and data spending. The report was compiled by private contractor TELCO Management.

"In the most recent report provided by the contractor, it became possible to view the official mobile phone number of parliamentarians and their staff even though they appeared redacted from the published files," a DPS spokesperson stated.

The department removed the documents immediately after being alerted to the problem and is investigating the cause with the contractor. While the exact number of affected individuals wasn't disclosed, Fairfax reported it reached into the hundreds.

The DPS has committed to addressing privacy concerns with affected MPs. TELCO Management has been contacted for comment.

# Britain Boycotts Russian Biathlon Event Over Doping Scandal

Britain has announced it will boycott a biathlon event in Tyumen, Russia, citing "brain-washed, deluded and dishonest comments" from Russian athletes following the damning McLaren report.

The report alleges that over 1,000 Russian athletes benefited from state-sponsored doping between 2011 and 2015, with 31 suspicious cases specifically involving biathletes according to the International Biathlon Union.

The IBU plans to announce sanctions on 22 December, following World Anti-Doping Agency guidelines. The investigation focused heavily on the Sochi Olympic Winter Games.

Britain joins the Czech Republic in boycotting the March 9-12 competition in Tyumen, taking a firm stance against what they perceive as inadequate responses from Russian sporting authorities.

# Ukraine Blocks Russian Websites and Services in Escalating Sanctions Row

Ukraine has dramatically escalated sanctions against Russia by blocking access to the country's most popular social media platforms and internet services, in a move that could affect millions of Ukrainian users.

President Petro Poroshenko has signed off on restrictions targeting major Russian digital platforms including the social networks VK.com and Odnoklassniki, search engine Yandex, and the Mail.ru email service. The decision represents a significant ramping up of sanctions on Ukraine's neighbour for its annexation of Crimea and the continuing conflict in eastern Ukraine.

Ukrainian service providers have been ordered to block access to these sites, whilst the companies' offices in Ukraine will face asset freezes and other restrictions. However, it remains unclear how the ban will be technically implemented and whether Ukrainian authorities possess the means to enforce it effectively.

The president's decision to implement recommendations from Ukraine's national security council could prove controversial domestically. VK (VKontakte) alone boasts an estimated 15 million users in Ukraine, whilst Odnoklassniki (translating as "Classmates") enjoys widespread popularity across the country.

Public reaction has been mixed. Blogger Anton Hodza welcomed the ban as a "fantastic opportunity" for Ukrainian start-ups to fill the void, whilst another commentator joked that authorities should brace for riots from disgruntled schoolchildren and pensioners. # Malta: A Journey Through Modern History from Colony to EU Member

Malta's modern history represents a remarkable transformation from British crown colony to independent republic and European Union member state, marked by pivotal moments of conflict, political upheaval, and strategic realignment.

## Colonial Era and World War II Heroism

Malta became a crown colony of the British Empire in 1814, establishing a relationship that would define the island nation for over a century. This connection proved crucial during World War II, when Malta's strategic Mediterranean location made it a vital Allied base and a primary target for Axis forces.

The German and Italian air forces subjected Malta to relentless bombing campaigns, testing the resilience of its population. In recognition of extraordinary civilian courage during these attacks, King George VI awarded the entire colony the George Cross in 1942, Britain's highest civilian decoration for heroism—a honor that remains part of Malta's national flag today.

## Path to Independence

Malta's journey toward self-governance proved circuitous. Self-government was first granted in 1947, only to be revoked in 1959 before being restored in 1962. Full independence finally arrived in 1964, launching a new chapter in Maltese history.

Under the Nationalist Party from 1964-71, Malta pursued pro-Western alignment. However, the 1971 election of Dom Mintoff's Malta Labour Party dramatically shifted the nation's trajectory toward non-alignment, cultivating special relationships with Libya and Communist states. Malta became a republic in 1974, and the closure of British military bases in 1979 symbolically ended the colonial era.

## Political Oscillation and European Integration

Malta's political landscape witnessed significant oscillation between parties with contrasting visions. After Mintoff's resignation in 1984, the Nationalist Party's 1987 victory under Eddie Fenech Adami signaled a pivot toward European integration.

Malta's diplomatic significance was highlighted when it hosted the historic 1989 summit between Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev and US President George Bush. The nation submitted its EU membership application in 1990, though this ambition was temporarily shelved when the Labour Party returned to power in 1996.

The Nationalist Party's 1998 return revived EU aspirations. In December 2002, Malta received formal invitation to join the EU, confirmed by a March 2003 referendum where 53% voted yes. Malta officially joined the EU in May 2004 as one of ten new member states.

## Contemporary Challenges

Lawrence Gonzi succeeded Adami as prime minister in 2004, overseeing Malta's euro adoption in January 2008. The 2008 elections saw the Nationalist Party retain power by a narrow margin.

Malta's predominantly Catholic identity was celebrated through papal visits in 2001 and 2009. In 2011, parliament legalized divorce following a referendum, ending Malta's status as Europe's only country banning the practice.

The 2012 financial crisis brought economic concerns, with credit downgrades and IMF warnings about contagion risks. Labour returned to power in March 2013 elections. That August, Malta faced international criticism when refusing docking rights to a tanker carrying rescued African migrants, highlighting ongoing Mediterranean migration challenges.

Malta's history demonstrates remarkable adaptability, navigating between great powers while forging its distinct identity in modern Europe.

# Hillsborough Inquests: Police 'Lost Control' Before Disaster, Court Hears

A retired police officer has told the Hillsborough inquests that control room staff "had basically lost control" on the day 96 Liverpool fans died in the 1989 stadium disaster.

Retired PC Trevor Bichard, one of five officers in the control room, was giving evidence at the new inquests. He also told the jury no-one inside the box was monitoring the central pens where the crush took place.

Ninety-six fans died following the crush at the FA Cup semi-final between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest.

Mr Bichard told the jury that after 15:00 BST on the day of the disaster, 15 April 1989, police radios were not working and "we had basically lost control".

"It was clear that we weren't controlling what was happening," he said. "The instruction had gone out to open the gates. Another message had come in about opening another gate. The situation had created a life of its own."

He told the inquests he began to receive radio messages about the volume of people outside the gates at the Leppings Lane end of the Sheffield stadium at 14:30. He turned one of the cameras to look at the crowd outside and estimated there were about 3,000 people there, the jury heard.

Mr Bichard, who retired after reaching the rank of chief inspector, said he focused completely on events taking place outside the turnstiles at Leppings Lane, not on the terraces.

He said one of the cameras, camera number five, which was overlooking the Leppings Lane terraces, was "iffy" and having "whiteouts". He said he was surprised when he overheard a "unique" order by Supt Roger Marshall to open exit gate C at the Leppings Lane end to relieve the crush outside, the jury heard.

Mr Bichard said the instruction was "insistent and desperate" and his voice was "very distressed". He said there was "no discussion" about where fans would go, and that he had "no idea" why he did not question where fans would go once it was opened. The gate was opened at 14:52.

"People would come in, choose where they wanted to stand and gradually it would fill out," he said. "Central pens always fill first and then it moves outwards," Mr Bichard told the inquests. He said that the concern was about the people outside. "Leppings Lane was left in these particular type of circumstances to find its own level," he said.

Mr Bichard also told the jury of a brief discussion, lasting only seconds between 14:30 and 14:45, in which senior officers talked about delaying the kick-off.

"I would describe it as Sgt [Michael] Goddard saying 'The policy is that we don't delay the kick off if the fans have chosen to come late, if there's a road accident' and [Supt] Bernard Murray saying to [Ch Sup] David Duckenfield 'Yes, that's right'," he said.

The inquests continue.

# China Secures Major Diplomatic Victory as 50 Nations Sign AIIB Agreement

Washington had attempted to persuade its allies to refrain from joining, but those efforts ultimately proved unsuccessful.

The AIIB, initially created in October by 21 countries under Chinese leadership, will finance Asian energy, transport, and infrastructure projects. Seven additional countries are expected to sign by year's end, bringing the total membership to 57 nations from Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America.

## Economic and Strategic Implications

Beyond diplomatic significance, the AIIB serves crucial economic objectives for Beijing. As China seeks to redirect its engineering capabilities abroad, the bank provides a mechanism to finance infrastructure development throughout Asia. "Answer - lend the region the money to pay Chinese companies to build a 21st Century Asia according to a Beijing master plan and with Chinese influence at its core," explained one analyst.

The BBC's Martin Patience notes this is one of several institutions China has established to advance its economic agenda, driven largely by frustration over its limited influence in established global financial institutions like the World Bank.

## Financial Structure

The AIIB will commence operations with authorized capital of $50 billion (£31.8 billion), eventually expanding to $100 billion. According to China's Finance Ministry, Beijing will hold the largest stake at 30.34%, translating to 26.06% of voting rights within the multilateral institution.

India will serve as the second-largest shareholder with a projected 10-15% stake, while Russia and Germany will occupy the third and fourth positions respectively.

## Shifting Global Power Dynamics

One British official candidly observed: "If an alien landed on earth they would be puzzled by its international financial institutions as China is grossly underrepresented." Many observers suggest the AIIB's rapid development might not have occurred had the US successfully reformed existing institutions to accommodate China's growing economic clout.

After three decades of remarkable growth, China's representation in international financial institutions no longer reflects global economic realities. Under President Xi Jinping, this initiative demonstrates China's determination to assert itself as a major power on the world stage.

Chinese Finance Minister Lou Jiwei expressed confidence on Monday that the AIIB could begin functioning before year's end, according to Reuters.

# Horse Rider Thrown After Chinook Helicopter Flyover in Bradford-on-Avon

A staff member at a Wiltshire riding stable was injured when a military Chinook helicopter caused her horse to panic during a training exercise.

Vicky Fielding, 20, suffered bruising after being thrown from her horse at Hudds Farm in Bradford-on-Avon when the aircraft flew overhead last Friday. "She panicked straight away and there was nothing I could do," Ms Fielding said. "I'll be anxious if I hear another Chinook coming over."

Bernice Marshallsay, the yard's owner, said whilst she was aware of military exercises in the area, the stable received no advance warning about the low-flying aircraft. "We get no information at all and I've complained to the MoD on at least two other occasions and it still keeps happening," she said. "Somebody's going to be seriously injured before something's done about this."

A Ministry of Defence spokesman said it was raising aircrews' awareness of horse riders and doing all it can to minimise disturbance to the public whilst crews train for operational duty.

# Manchester City Close to Signing Claudio Bravo as Joe Hart's Future Remains Uncertain

Manchester City are on the verge of completing the signing of Barcelona goalkeeper Claudio Bravo, with the Chile international having arrived in Manchester on Tuesday afternoon to finalise the deal.

City manager Pep Guardiola, while refusing to officially confirm the transfer, acknowledged the widespread reports when he said: "I cannot deny what everyone knows. The deal is not complete. After I will answer about a player who at the moment is not our player."

The imminent arrival of Bravo has cast further doubt over the future of England's number one goalkeeper Joe Hart, who has not featured for City this season despite being fit and available. However, in what could be seen as a lifeline for the 29-year-old, Guardiola confirmed that Hart will start Wednesday's Champions League qualifier second leg against Steaua Bucharest at the Etihad Stadium.

Barcelona have reportedly given Bravo, 33, permission to leave the Nou Camp, paving the way for his move to the Premier League champions. The goalkeeper's expertise with the ball at his feet aligns perfectly with Guardiola's tactical philosophy, which demands a 'sweeper-keeper' capable of initiating attacks from the back.

Hart began this campaign as second choice behind Willy Caballero, a clear indication of Guardiola's doubts about his suitability for the role. The former Barcelona and Bayern Munich manager has been forthright about his requirements from a goalkeeper, explaining his tactical approach in detail on Tuesday.

"From 15 years old, I grew up knowing every time we had a good build-up we created chances," Guardiola said. "When the goalkeeper, the full-backs and the centre-backs can do this, it is easier. The pitch is big and the space is always there."

He added: "I would like to have the ball for 90 minutes. I know some managers prefer to play on the counter-attack. I am completely the opposite."

Despite training with the first-team squad on Tuesday morning at the City Football Academy, Hart's long-term future at the club remains uncertain. While it was widely expected that he would leave before the transfer window closes on 31 August, an immediate departure now appears less certain.

Hart has reportedly rejected potential moves to both Sevilla and Borussia Dortmund, who have expressed interest in signing him. Everton, who seemed a likely destination last week, have apparently cooled their interest due to Hart's substantial wages, which exceed their current salary structure, and the impressive early-season performances of their new signing Maarten Stekelenburg.

England manager Sam Allardyce has expressed concern about Hart's situation but confirmed he would still select the goalkeeper for the World Cup qualifier against Slovakia on 4 September, provided his lack of club football doesn't continue.

Hart wasn't the only high-profile player training away from the main group on Tuesday. Yaya Toure, Wilfried Bony, Samir Nasri, and Eliaquim Mangala, none of whom have featured for City this season, were among 33 players training across two pitches at the academy.

With just over two weeks remaining in the transfer window, Hart faces a crucial decision about his future as Guardiola's revolution at Manchester City continues to gather pace.

# Train Hits Conveyor Wagon at 102mph in Barrow upon Soar Incident

An East Midlands Trains service travelling from Leicester to York struck part of a conveyor wagon at Barrow upon Soar earlier this month, prompting dual investigations by safety authorities.

The collision occurred at 10:27 on 14 February when the train, travelling at 102mph, hit the boom of a conveyor wagon protruding over the line at Mountsorrel sidings. The Rail Accident Investigation Branch (RAIB) confirmed the train was within the 110mph speed limit for that section.

The driver immediately applied emergency brakes, preventing derailment and passenger injuries, though the driver was reportedly "badly shaken" by the incident.

A man working on the lorry was taken to hospital for treatment. Following the collision, the train proceeded at low speed to Loughborough, where passengers transferred to alternative services to complete their journeys.

Both the RAIB and the Office of Road and Rail have launched investigations into the incident to determine the circumstances that led to the equipment obstructing the railway line.

# Drug Dealer Sentenced for Supplying Hallucinogen That Led to Fatal Stabbing

A drug dealer who supplied a dangerous hallucinogenic substance that led to a young man being stabbed to death has been sentenced to community service.

Keiron Turley, 20, from Malden Road in Liverpool, was ordered to complete 200 hours of unpaid community work at York Crown Court after pleading guilty to being concerned in the supply of class A drugs. North Yorkshire Police confirmed Turley had supplied 25i-NBOMe, commonly known as N-bomb, to victim Liam Miller in June 2015.

The hallucinogenic drug triggered a fatal chain of events culminating in Mr Miller's death the following month. Samuel Donley, then 19, stabbed his close friend 32 times during a psychotic episode at his home on Hamilton Drive, York, on the night of July 27 whilst his parents were away.

During Donley's trial at Leeds Crown Court, jurors heard he believed he was trapped in a dream and thought Mr Miller was a skull that needed to be stabbed to return to reality. Donley, now 20, was jailed last November for six years and eight months after admitting manslaughter.

He also received a concurrent 32-month sentence for wounding innocent passer-by Theophilos Theophilou during what detectives described as a "horrific and violent attack."

Mr Miller was from Terrington, near Malton.

# UK Services Sector Growth Slows as Business Confidence Weakens

The UK services sector experienced a notable slowdown in December, according to the latest Markit/CIPS purchasing managers' index (PMI), though the economy continues to expand at a healthy rate.

The services PMI fell to 55.5 from 59.9 in November, marking a significant drop but remaining comfortably above the 50-point threshold that separates growth from contraction. Despite the deceleration, Markit reported that UK growth had "stabilised at a solid pace" with continued strong increases in new business.

Chris Williamson, chief economist at Markit, noted that "the services sector remained the key driver of the UK's economic upturn in December, helping to offset the recent weakness seen in manufacturing and putting the economy on the starting block for another year of 2 to 2.5% growth in 2016."

The data suggests the economy grew by 0.5% in the fourth quarter, slightly down from Markit's previous estimate of 0.6%. This follows mixed signals from other sectors, with manufacturing growing at its slowest pace in three months whilst construction rebounded due to stronger commercial building activity.

However, Mr Williamson warned of "significant downside risks" facing the UK economy in 2016, including the impact of the Living Wage, government spending cuts, potential interest rate increases, global economic concerns, and uncertainty over Brexit.

Concerns are mounting as job creation in the services sector slowed to its weakest pace in five months during December. Long-term business expectations also fell to their lowest level since 2013, which Mr Williamson described as "a warning shot to those taking a complacent view of economic prospects for the coming year."

# NHS 111 Service Rollout Should Be Halted, Says BMA Chief

The troubled rollout of the NHS 111 helpline should be suspended immediately due to serious safety concerns, the British Medical Association has warned.

The new telephone service, designed to replace NHS Direct, is being piloted across various regions of England but has encountered significant problems, with some callers reportedly left waiting on hold for hours before receiving medical advice.

Dr Laurence Buckman, chair of the BMA's GP committee, has called for the wider implementation of the service to be stalled until the numerous technical and operational issues can be resolved. "The BMA is seriously concerned that these failures are not only having impact on other, already overstretched NHS services, but potentially putting patient safety at risk," he said.

The association has received widespread reports of NHS 111 failures from multiple pilot areas. Several regions have struggled to cope with call volumes, while others have experienced catastrophic IT system failures. In Greater Manchester, the entire system crashed, leaving calls completely unanswered. One elderly patient was forced to wait 90 minutes for a callback from the service.

These problems have triggered a surge in ambulance callouts and accident and emergency department visits, as frustrated callers resort to alternative measures to access healthcare professionals. This has placed additional strain on already stretched NHS resources.

"Patients need to have their calls answered immediately and correctly and not be faced with any form of delay," Dr Buckman emphasized. "The Department of Health needs to reconsider immediately its launch of NHS 111 which clearly is not functioning properly. They must ensure that the system is safe for patients before it is rolled out any further."

The Department of Health has acknowledged the difficulties and is providing some areas with additional time to prepare. It has already approved extensions of up to six months beyond the original 1 April 2013 deadline for regions struggling to establish the new service.

Health Minister Lord Howe defended the rollout, stating: "NHS 111 will help patients access the whole of the NHS through just one simple number. To ensure that patients get the best care and treatment, we are giving some areas more time to go live with NHS 111 while we carry out thorough testing to ensure that those services are reliable."

The existing NHS Direct 0845 4647 service will continue operating in areas where NHS 111 is not yet available, including North of Tyne and Tees, North Essex, Bedfordshire and Luton, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, Leicestershire and Rutland, Berkshire, Cornwall and Devon.

# BMW Masters: Play Suspended as Slattery Leads in Shanghai

Twenty-three players will return early on Monday to complete their rounds after play was suspended on Sunday because of bad light at the BMW Masters in Shanghai.

England's Andrew Slattery and South Korea's Soomin Lee are 14-under after 13 completed holes, sharing the lead in difficult conditions. Co-leader Alexander Levy of France faces a birdie putt on the 13th green when play resumes.

More than six and a half hours were lost to bad weather over the first two days, and more time was lost in the final round on Sunday because of an afternoon thunderstorm.

Australian Scott Hend is the clubhouse leader at 13-under after a bogey-free 66, with South African Brandon Stone and Dutchman Joost Luiten also 13-under with five and three holes to complete respectively.

# Northern Ireland Health Minister Issues New Abortion Guidelines Following Human Rights Ruling

Northern Ireland's Health Minister Simon Hamilton has announced plans to introduce new guidelines on abortion following a landmark court ruling that declared the region's current legislation to be in breach of human rights law.

The announcement comes after a judicial review on Monday found that the grounds for abortion should be extended in Northern Ireland. Currently, termination of pregnancy is only permitted if a woman's life is at risk or there is a permanent or serious risk to her mental or physical health.

The Northern Ireland Human Rights Commission (NIHRC), which brought the case, is seeking to extend abortion access to cases of serious foetal malformation, rape or incest. Unlike the rest of the United Kingdom, the 1967 Abortion Act does not apply to Northern Ireland.

Minister Hamilton confirmed that the new guidelines have been prepared in consultation with health professionals and would be made public after consideration by his Executive colleagues. "I think the guidelines offer an opportunity to clarify satisfactorily the law as it currently stands in Northern Ireland," he stated.

In Monday's ruling, Mr Justice Horner determined that women who were victims of sexual crimes and cases of fatal foetal abnormality were entitled to exemptions in the law. He stated that given the Northern Ireland Executive's unlikely action on the matter, and that citizens were entitled to have their human rights protected, the current legislation violated their rights under the European Convention on Human Rights.

The decision has been welcomed by Sarah Ewart, whose personal experience brought the issue to public attention in 2013. At 20 weeks pregnant, Ms Ewart was forced to travel to England for an abortion after her baby was diagnosed with anencephaly, a condition where the brain fails to develop.

Speaking on Tuesday, Ms Ewart expressed relief that women could now "get medical attention in our hospitals in our own country." She added: "At the start we'll just take small steps and see where we go from here."

However, Northern Ireland's Attorney General John Larkin said he was "profoundly disappointed" by the decision and was considering grounds for appeal.

The Lord Chief Justice's Office has indicated that whilst the court cannot force legislation to be changed, the final decision rests with Parliament.

# New Bus Station and Cycle Hub Planned for Cardiff's Central Square

A major transport development could transform Cardiff's Central Square, with plans for a 14-stand bus station and a 502-space cycle hub on the site of Marland House and NCP car park.

The proposal, scheduled for review by Cardiff council's planning committee on Wednesday, also includes retail units, a five-storey office block, a nine-storey apartment block, and a private car park.

The development comes after the city's previous bus station was demolished to accommodate BBC Wales' new headquarters at Central Square.

# Interpol Suspends €20 Million Fifa Partnership Over Corruption Scandal

Interpol has frozen a €20 million (£14m) agreement with Fifa, suspending a major anti-corruption partnership as the football governing body faces mounting allegations of bribery and wrongdoing.

The international police agency announced it would halt the 10-year "Integrity in Sport" programme, which was established in 2011 with Fifa funding to combat match-fixing and illegal gambling in football.

Juergen Stock, Interpol's Secretary General, said the decision was made "in light of the current context surrounding Fifa," adding that the organisation remains committed to integrity in sport but cannot continue the partnership under present circumstances.

"All external partners, whether public or private, must share the fundamental values and principles of the organisation, as well as those of the wider law enforcement community," Mr Stock stated.

The original agreement stipulated that Fifa must be "compatible with the principles, aims and activities of Interpol" – a condition now apparently in question.

Fifa expressed disappointment at the decision, with a spokesperson telling the BBC that the programme's "success and importance cannot be understated" and describing it as "a key part of addressing the transnational problem of match-fixing."

The football body argued the programme is "unrelated to the current issues surrounding Fifa" and warned that Interpol's "unilateral decision will negatively impact the fight against criminal activity." Fifa said it would reach out to Interpol for further discussions.

The suspension comes after US and Swiss authorities launched investigations into Fifa for alleged corruption. Last month, 14 current and former Fifa officials and sports marketing executives were charged following a years-long US-led investigation.

The scandal has cast doubt over the legitimacy of bidding processes for the 2018 and 2022 World Cups, awarded to Russia and Qatar respectively, with ongoing questions about potential irregularities in the selection process.

# Diageo to Move Scotch Whisky Bottling Jobs from Scotland to Italy

Drinks giant Diageo has announced plans to transfer some Scotch whisky bottling operations from Scotland to Italy, putting more than 100 jobs at risk across two Scottish plants.

Seventy jobs are expected to go at Shieldhall by the end of the year and 35 at Leven, unless new bottling contracts can be won. Diageo's bottling plant in Italy is running below capacity after it disposed of its wine business.

Unions at the main distiller of Scotch whisky strongly criticised the move. Unite said it was a "shocking betrayal of Scottish workers" and the GMB said it was connected to the economic uncertainties arising from Brexit.

But Diageo said it followed a review of its spirits bottling business to ensure the company delivered "leading performance" in domestic and export supply chains.

A spokesman added: "Regrettably, these changes may impact some roles in our European bottling plants towards the end of the year and we will now enter a period of consultation with our employees and their representatives to discuss the proposals in more detail.

"We are committed to our three spirits bottling sites in Europe - two in Scotland and one in Italy. The outcomes of this review will ensure we have the flexibility to respond to increased competition and external volatility, alongside testing and building the capability we need across our global supply chain to grow our brands."

There are currently 500 workers at Shieldhall, in south-west Glasgow, and 800 at Leven in Fife.

Cabinet Secretary for Finance Derek Mackay said Diageo's announcement was "deeply disappointing news". He said Scottish Enterprise is engaging with the company to explore all possible options for supporting those affected.

"If any redundancies proceed, through our initiative for responding to redundancy situations, Partnership Action for Continuing Employment, we will provide skills development and employability support to minimise the time that individuals affected are out of work."

# Shkreli to Invoke Fifth Amendment at Congressional Hearing on Drug Pricing

Martin Shkreli, the controversial former pharmaceutical executive, will refuse to testify before Congress about dramatic drug price increases, his attorney has confirmed.

Mr Shkreli's lawyer informed the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform that he would invoke his right against self-incrimination. The former hedge fund manager hit the headlines when his company raised the price of a life-saving drug by 5,000%. He also faces separate criminal charges that he defrauded investors.

The committee sent a letter to Mr Shkreli requesting he testify about his former company Turing Pharmaceuticals' decision to raise the price of the drug Daraprim, used to treat life-threatening parasitic infections.

In a statement, Congressman Elijah Cummings, a member of the committee said: "If he [Mr Shkreli] plans on trying to use his own intentional inaction as some kind of bogus excuse for not showing up at Tuesday's hearing, people will see right through such a juvenile tactic."

On Wednesday, Mr Shkreli posted a picture of the subpoena letter on his Twitter account and wrote, "Found this letter. Looks important."

In December, Mr Shkreli was arrested in New York on charges he defrauded investors at a drug company he previously ran, Retrophin, and a hedge fund, MSMB Capital Management, where he was a fund manager. He has denied the charges and was released on bail pending the trial.

The FBI allege Mr Shkreli "engaged in multiple schemes to ensnare investors through a web of lies and deceit". Neither of those cases are connected to Daraprim's price increase or Turing Pharmaceuticals. Mr Shkreli stepped down as Turing's head after his December arrest.

# Countryfile Success Leads to New BBC Daytime Spin-Off Series

The BBC has announced a new daytime spin-off of its hit rural affairs programme Countryfile, following the show's impressive ratings performance in 2015.

The Sunday night programme attracted an average of six million viewers throughout 2015, with a November episode reaching a peak audience of 7.8 million. In a significant achievement, Countryfile managed to beat The X Factor's Sunday results show in the ratings on two occasions last month.

The new five-part series, titled Countryfile Diaries, will launch in spring on BBC One. Running across a week, the spin-off will showcase country life through the changing seasons and will be scheduled to coincide with Countryfile's seasonal specials.

BBC daytime controller Dan McGolpin said the programme would allow viewers "to further enjoy the full splendour and sheer variety of life in the British countryside during key moments of the year".

Countryfile, presented by Matt Baker, Anita Rani and others, achieved its highest audiences in autumn when scheduled before Strictly Come Dancing. Between 8 November and 13 December, more than 7.2 million households tuned in on average.

Executive producer Bill Lyons attributed the "huge audience" to "the enduring love-affair between the British people and their countryside", making it the most popular weekly factual series on television.

Details of locations and presenters for Countryfile Diaries are yet to be announced.

# Yemen Peace Talks Announced as Conflict Intensifies with Rebel Attacks on Saudi Arabia

UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon has called for peace negotiations in Yemen as violence escalated dramatically on Saturday, with Houthi rebels launching increasingly bold attacks against Saudi Arabian targets.

The announcement of upcoming talks comes amid intensifying hostilities that have already claimed more than 2,000 lives over several months of warfare. Mr. Ban urged all parties to enter negotiations in good faith and without pre-conditions, though observers note this may prove challenging given the current climate.

In a significant escalation on Saturday, Saudi Arabia intercepted a Scud missile fired by Houthi rebels and their allies using a Patriot missile battery near the southwestern city of Khamis Mushait. According to the state-run Saudi Press Agency, this marked one of the few missile attacks since the air campaign began ten weeks ago.

A pro-Houthi military spokesman told Yemen's rebel-controlled Saba news agency that the missile targeted the Prince Khaled air base. The attack followed Friday's border clashes that left four Saudi soldiers and several Yemeni rebels dead.

BBC Middle East Editor Sebastian Usher notes that both Yemen's government—now largely exiled in Saudi Arabia—and the rebel forces have confirmed their attendance at peace negotiations. However, each side appears to be positioning for advantage before talks commence.

"The Houthis and their allies are launching ever bolder attacks inside Saudi Arabia to demonstrate they have withstood two months of air bombardment, while the Saudis only pound them more," Usher observed.

Saudi officials characterized the rebel actions as attempts "to penetrate our borders," which were ultimately repelled. The kingdom's 10-week bombing campaign has prioritized destroying rebel missile capabilities, though officials acknowledge the difficulty of this task, as approximately 300 missiles are believed hidden in caves.

The Saudi-led air campaign supports Yemeni President Abedrabbo Manour Hadi, who fled to Riyadh when Houthi forces advanced on his southern stronghold in Aden.

Meanwhile, the humanitarian situation continues to deteriorate dramatically. The UN has described the crisis as "catastrophic," with 20 million civilians—representing 80% of Yemen's population—requiring humanitarian assistance.

Despite the escalating violence and mounting civilian toll, the scheduled peace talks represent a potential diplomatic breakthrough in the conflict.

# Prison Lifer Convicted of Murdering Fellow Inmate with Kitchen Knife

A prisoner already serving life for murder has been found guilty of killing a fellow inmate at Dartmoor Prison with a 10-inch kitchen knife.

William Tolcher, 51, denied attacking Alex Cusworth, 37, with the 10in (23cm) knife at Dartmoor Prison last November. A jury at Plymouth Crown Court found him guilty of murder and he is due to be sentenced on Friday.

Tolcher, from Liverpool, is serving a life sentence for the murder of a woman in Newquay, Cornwall, in 1996.

Mr Cusworth suffered internal bleeding after the attack and died at Derriford Hospital in Plymouth.

Judge James Dingemens said he was considering a minimum 30-year jail sentence.

Tolcher was convicted of murdering a woman in Newquay, Cornwall, in 1996 and was already serving a life sentence.

# Inmate Admits Attacking Soham Killer Ian Huntley's Attacker

A prisoner has admitted attempting to murder the man who previously attacked Soham murderer Ian Huntley.

Kevin McCarthy, 49, appeared at Cambridge Crown Court charged with the attempted murder of Damien Fowkes, 41, leaving him with life-threatening neck injuries on 2 October. Both men were inmates at HMP Whitemoor in Cambridgeshire at the time. McCarthy is due to be sentenced on Wednesday.

Fowkes is serving a life sentence with a minimum term of 20 years for the attempted murder of Huntley at HMP Frankland in Durham in 2010. Fowkes went on to strangle paedophile and child-killer Colin Hatch in 2011 at Full Sutton high security prison near York.

# Berlin Police Shut Down Dandy Diner Opening After Massive Crowd Forms

The highly anticipated opening of the Dandy Diner in Berlin was abruptly shut down by police after drawing an unprecedented crowd on Saturday night.

About 300 people packed inside the new restaurant while hundreds more waited outside, prompting police intervention. The Dandy Diary blog on Facebook confirmed the closure with a colourful expletive, acknowledging "police closed us down."

The event, organized by entrepreneurs Jakob Haupt and David Roth, attracted exceptional attention. German newspaper Der Tagesspiegel noted that restaurant openings "have rarely drawn such a big crowd" in Berlin.

The massive gathering extended far down Karl Marx Strasse in the Neukoelln district, creating significant buzz on social media.

# Strictly Come Dancing Final: Four Couples Compete for Glitterball Trophy

The stage is set for one of the most anticipated television events of the year as four remaining couples prepare to battle it out in the Strictly Come Dancing final this Saturday. Actresses Kellie Bright and Georgia May Foote, presenter Katie Derham, and pop star Jay McGuiness are all hoping to dance their way to glory alongside their professional partners, with the ultimate prize being the iconic Strictly glitterball trophy.

In interviews with the BBC, all four finalists expressed a mixture of excitement and emotion as they prepare for their final performances. The pressure is mounting as they face the culmination of weeks of intensive training and live performances that have captivated audiences throughout the series.

The final comes after last week's dramatic dance-off, which saw presenter Anita Rani and her partner Gleb Savchenko eliminated from the competition. The judges unanimously voted to save Katie Derham and her partner Anton Du Beke, sending them through to the final and making Strictly history in the process.

Katie Derham spoke about the significance of taking Anton to the final for the first time in his 12-year tenure on the show. Despite this achievement, she maintained a realistic perspective about their chances of winning. "I don't know if anybody has really thought about the trophy much," she said. She revealed that a friend had given her a miniature glitterball necklace with the message: "Even if you don't win you have your own little one already."

EastEnders star Kellie Bright admitted to feeling "slightly more emotional" ahead of the final show but said she was focusing on the opportunity to relax afterwards. "I'm quite looking forward to not having any make-up on, or brushing my hair, or even getting out of my pyjamas for a few days," she confessed. She emphasized that winning wasn't her primary focus, saying: "Our whole thing has always been to try and entertain everybody, so that's what we want to do on Saturday."

Former Coronation Street actress Georgia May Foote said she was "more excited than nervous," though she acknowledged the added pressure of the final, describing it as "everything you have learnt put together."

In a surprising revelation, pop star Jay McGuiness announced he would not be repeating his memorable jive in the final, despite fan expectations. "I think the jive was so fun and I think everyone loved it. I'm more than happy with what that was [but] I'd rather do something that I think will surprise people," he explained. McGuiness also expressed his newfound passion for the show, saying: "I'm in love with the show, I think it's awesome."

The final will consist of two live shows on Saturday. One couple will be eliminated at the beginning of the second show, with the remaining three finalists performing their favourite dance of the series before the winner is crowned. All professional dancers and celebrity participants will reunite for the spectacular finale, with several posting excited messages and rehearsal photos on social media.

Strictly Come Dancing airs on BBC One at 18:35 GMT and 21:00 GMT.

# Storm Collapses Circus Tent in New Hampshire, Injuring Spectators

A violent storm with winds reaching up to 60mph struck a circus tent in Lancaster, New Hampshire, on Monday evening, injuring multiple people as a performance was just beginning.

Approximately 100 spectators were inside the tent when the storm hit, causing the structure to collapse. Although a thunderstorm warning was in effect for the region, it remains unclear whether attendees were aware of the storm's severity before entering the venue.

Eyewitness Heidi Medeiros, attending with her three-year-old son, described the terrifying moments as the tent went dark and screams erupted. "I see these very large metal poles that are in the ground and go through the top of the tent, I see them starting to come out of the ground and fly up, into the air toward us," she told WMUR-TV.

Medeiros and her son escaped injury, though the flying poles came within feet of their seats. The injured were transported to local hospitals for treatment.

The incident comes just one day after a similar tragedy in Illinois, where a music festival tent collapsed during a storm, killing one person and injuring more than a dozen others.

**Mel Giedroyc on Strictly Come Dancing: "I'd Want to Be Ann Widdecombe"**

Television presenter Mel Giedroyc has revealed why she's hesitant about appearing on Strictly Come Dancing, despite being a devoted fan of the BBC show.

"I love watching it so much I almost didn't want to spoil the pleasure by being on it," she told Radio Times. The 48-year-old said it was tricky for a woman her age to be on the show. "You're not the comedy old bag yet, which would be the joy of going on Strictly," she said. "If I did it, I'd want to be Ann Widdecombe. I'd want to be out there getting the laughs, being dragged around."

The presenter may not have strutted her stuff in a ball gown, but she can still be seen on a prime time Saturday night show - fronting BBC One's talent search Let It Shine.

The gig comes after Giedroyc stepped down as co-host of the Great British Bake Off, along with Sue Perkins, when it was announced the hit show was moving to Channel 4.

Giedroyc said the furore surrounding the move was "a pretty weird time". "The press were camped out on my doorstep. My eldest daughter actually saw a few of them off, which I was very, very proud of," she said.

"I'm not the kind of person who would court that sort of attention. I have a very private existence and I had to slightly clench my buttocks during that."
