# Islamic State: Syria Regime Buying Oil from IS, Says US

Islamic State's primary customer for oil has been the Syrian government of President Bashar al-Assad, despite the regime's fight against the militant group, a senior US Treasury official has revealed.

Adam Szubin told the BBC that the two sides were engaged in millions of dollars of trade while simultaneously trying to destroy each other. He estimated that IS was making up to $40 million monthly from oil sales, including to buyers in Turkey.

The group has also looted approximately $1 billion from banks in territories under its control, Mr Szubin added.

The US-led coalition has been conducting airstrikes against IS targets in Syria and Iraq for over a year, recently killing the group's finance chief. A new military campaign called Tidal Wave 2 has intensified strikes on oil infrastructure, including fields, refineries, and tankers.

Mr Szubin emphasised that disrupting IS's cash flow was crucial to the coalition's strategy. Unlike other terrorist organisations, IS doesn't depend on foreign donations but generates revenue from its own operations.

According to UK defence consultancy IHS, IS currently earns around $80 million monthly, primarily from oil revenues. Additional income sources include taxation, smuggling of drugs and antiquities, robbery, kidnapping, and electricity sales.

The revelation highlights the complex and controversial economic relationships in the Syrian conflict, where sworn enemies continue trading despite their military confrontation. Cutting these financial lifelines remains a key objective for coalition forces fighting the militant group.

# Man Charged with Murder of Woman Found Dead in Neath Home

A 43-year-old man has appeared in court charged with murdering a woman found dead at a property in South Wales.

Andrea Lewis, 51, was discovered at a home on Fairyland Road in Tonna, Neath, at approximately 08:00 GMT on 30 January.

Rhys Trevor Anthony Hobbs, 43, from Tonna, appeared at Swansea Crown Court on Friday charged with her murder. He was remanded in custody until his next court appearance on 24 March.

A second man, aged 46, who was also arrested in connection with Ms Lewis's death, has been released on police bail.

# Creepy Clown Sightings Spread Across Six States, Alarming Communities

A wave of unsettling clown sightings has swept across at least six U.S. states, with reports of mysterious figures dressed as clowns attempting to lure children and lurking in wooded areas, prompting police warnings and community concern.

The most recent incident occurred in Georgia, where two young boys fled in terror while waiting for their school bus. "We saw a man with all black on, clown mask, and a red wig," 12-year-old Cameron Frails told WRDW News, describing their frightening encounter.

In nearby Aiken County, South Carolina, police responded to an equally disturbing report captured on radio dispatch: "Subject dressed in a red and yellow suit with a clown mask through the woods. He also had a green laser light shining it through windows."

The phenomenon has now spread to Ohio, South Carolina, North Carolina, California, Wisconsin, and Georgia, with children claiming the clowns have tried to lure them into the woods using money.

"The clowning around needs to stop," declared Greenville, South Carolina Police Chief Ken Miller at a press conference earlier this month. "It's illegal, it's dangerous, it's inappropriate, it's creating community concern."

Law enforcement officials have warned that even if these incidents are pranks, criminal charges may still be filed against perpetrators.

New Jersey State Police addressed the trend on Facebook with a creepy clown photo, writing: "For all of the coulrophobics out there, we apologise for the pic, but it was necessary. If all of the bad people out there stuck out as much as a person dressed as a clown, we wouldn't have write posts like this."

The sightings have distressed legitimate clown performers, who already contend with negative depictions like Stephen King's character Pennywise from "IT" and serial killer John Wayne Gacy, who performed as an amateur clown. At least one Georgia performer has begun informing police of his movements whenever in costume to avoid causing public alarm.

# Italian City Government Dissolved Over Mafia Links

In an unprecedented move, Italian authorities have dismissed the entire city government of a provincial capital over suspected ties to the notorious 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate, Interior Minister Annamaria Cancellieri announced.

Mayor Demetrio Arena and all 30 city councillors were removed from office to prevent "mafia contagion" within the local administration. This marks the first time an entire provincial capital government has been dissolved due to suspected mafia connections, though smaller municipalities have faced similar action previously.

Three government-appointed commissioners will oversee city operations for 18 months until new elections can be held.

The dramatic intervention follows months of concern about 'Ndrangheta influence over the city council. An investigation was triggered after one councillor was arrested last year on charges of association with the criminal organization.

According to experts, the 'Ndrangheta has surpassed Sicily's Cosa Nostra to become one of the world's largest criminal enterprises. The organization generates vast revenues primarily through cocaine trafficking, extortion, and money laundering operations.

Italy's parliamentary anti-mafia commission considers the 'Ndrangheta the country's most dangerous and wealthiest mafia group. The syndicate has successfully expanded its influence beyond its Calabrian stronghold by exploiting migration patterns of southern Italians moving northward and abroad.

The dissolution demonstrates Italian authorities' determination to combat organized crime's infiltration of democratic institutions.

# West Brom Fans Organize Collection for Chris Brunt After Coin-Throwing Incident

West Bromwich Albion supporters are rallying to show their appreciation for defender Chris Brunt following an incident in which he was struck by a coin thrown by one of the club's own fans.

The incident occurred after Brunt had gone to give his shirt to a visiting fan after Albion lost 3-1 in the FA Cup fifth round at Championship side Reading on Saturday.

A group of fans will hold collections outside The Hawthorns before Saturday's league game against Crystal Palace.

"We want to show Albion fans are not all like that," said fan Debbie Green.

Brunt, 31, said he was "disgusted" and "ashamed" after being struck on the face by a coin thrown by a West Brom supporter.

"I was angry with the result but no way would you throw anything," Green, 54, who was at Reading and is helping to organise the collection, told BBC Sport.

"After the game, Chris was the only one who walked up to the fans and clapped them.

"I was about 25 feet away from what happened. Most were clapping him back and then you get this one idiot.

"Chris had given his shirt to a little girl. He didn't deserve that to happen to him.

"I have supported Albion for 50 years but I was ashamed to be an Albion fan on Saturday."

Up to 30 Albion fans have come forward so far to hold buckets outside the ground and go into pubs near The Hawthorns. All money raised will go to a charity of the Northern Ireland international's choice, added Green.

A West Brom spokesman said: "It's a fan-led initiative and we are trying to co-ordinate it. It's got the club's blessing and it's got Chris's blessing."

West Brom will feature an image of long-serving Brunt on the front cover of Saturday's programme above the word 'loyalty'.

Brunt, who can also play in midfield, joined West Brom from Sheffield Wednesday in 2007 and has played 313 games for the club.

# Nigeria Deploys Female Police to Displacement Camps After Abuse Allegations

Nigerian authorities have deployed female police officers to camps housing people displaced by Boko Haram violence, following allegations of sexual abuse by security personnel.

State police commissioner Damian Chukwu said the female officers will ensure the protection of women in the camps. The deployment comes after a Human Rights Watch (HRW) report last week alleged that several women had been sexually abused by security officers.

The officers, drawn from various divisions, are also tasked to "dig out true happenings" in the camps, Mr Chukwu told the Nigerian News Agency.

President Muhammadu Buhari said he was "worried" and "shocked" about the HRW report and ordered an investigation into the alleged abuses.

The report detailed how women and girls had been coerced into sex and abandoned when they became pregnant. "It is disgraceful and outrageous that people who should protect these women and girls are attacking and abusing them," said HRW's Mausi Segun.

The group blamed the vulnerability of women - many of whom are widows and unaccompanied orphans - on irregular supplies of food, clothing, medicine and other essentials in internally displaced camps in Borno state capital, Maiduguri.

Boko Haram's seven-year battle to create an Islamic state has forced thousands from their homes.

# Security Review Recommended for Stormont After Unauthorised Flag Incident

A comprehensive security review of Parliament Buildings has been recommended by police following an incident in which unauthorised nationalist flags were flown from the Stormont estate.

The tricolour and another nationalist flag appeared on flagpoles at the Belfast site earlier in June, with a republican group called the 1916 Societies claiming responsibility for hoisting them.

DUP assembly member Paula Bradley, who serves on the assembly commission, raised concerns in the assembly on Tuesday about potential security breaches. She questioned whether police had assessed the risk to Parliament Buildings and asked what measures were being implemented to ensure the building's safety had not been compromised.

In a written response on behalf of Chief Constable George Hamilton, a PSNI officer stated that whilst a full investigation into the incident is ongoing, police would recommend "a full review of internal security be undertaken under the auspices of the assembly commission".

The letter also revealed that Chief Superintendent Nigel Grimshaw has requested an immediate, updated threat assessment relating to Parliament Buildings and will review the findings once received.

An internal assembly investigation into the unauthorised flags was launched but subsequently suspended pending the outcome of the police inquiry. Assembly authorities have requested a report from contractors currently working on site, who are renovating sections of the roof and fourth floor.

The assembly confirmed that the flags were removed immediately upon discovery. The incident has raised serious questions about security protocols at one of Northern Ireland's most significant political buildings.

# Aston Villa Boss Remi Garde Apologises After Humiliating Liverpool Defeat

Aston Villa manager Remi Garde has apologised to supporters following his side's humiliating 6-0 home defeat to Liverpool, admitting his team "did not fight enough" in their battle against relegation.

The crushing loss marked the first time the Midlands club had conceded six goals at home in a league fixture since October 1983, deepening the crisis at Villa Park. The result leaves Villa rooted to the bottom of the Premier League, a seemingly insurmountable eight points from safety.

"I feel humiliated. I am sorry for the fans who came to Villa Park," said Garde after the match. "This is a bad feeling that we did not fight enough."

The manner of the defeat proved particularly concerning for the Frenchman. After conceding two goals before half-time, Villa capitulated spectacularly after the break, shipping four goals in just 13 minutes. The home supporters began streaming towards the exits during the second half, while those who remained directed their frustration at American owner Randy Lerner with chants of 'Lerner out'.

"Before the game you could expect the level of the two teams was not on the same one but, after quite a good 15 minutes, I don't know what happened," Garde explained. "The first two goals were difficult to digest and then my team did not play anymore. We were always two or three metres away from the opponent. It was very easy for them."

The Villa boss expressed particular disappointment at his side's lack of fighting spirit given their precarious position. "I was expecting fighting spirit, especially in the position we are in, but we were not able to deliver it."

Despite the demoralising defeat, Garde refused to concede that relegation is inevitable. The former Lyon manager, appointed in November on a three-and-a-half-year contract, insisted he would maintain belief whilst any mathematical hope remains.

"I was not expecting this kind of match and we have to go for the next one to win it," he said. "Until we have little hope, I will be the one who will still believe. After a game like this, it is very difficult but we won't play Liverpool every weekend."

Garde also addressed the supporters' frustrations, acknowledging the difficult situation at the club. "I understand [the fans' frustration]. I don't know exactly who let down who in this football club. I am trying to concentrate on my job and try to do the best with the players who want to still fight."

BBC Radio 5 live's Pat Murphy was scathing in his assessment, describing Villa as "an absolute shambles" and questioning what incentive Garde has to remain at the club given the lack of investment and the scale of the challenge facing him.

# JCB Chairman Pledges £100,000 to Save Wedgwood Museum Collection

JCB chairman Sir Anthony Bamford has donated £100,000 towards the appeal to save the historic Wedgwood Museum collection, citing the company's "deep roots and long links with manufacturing in Staffordshire".

The Art Fund announced it has raised more than £2.3m following an "extraordinary tide" of recent donations. The organisation needs £2.74m by 30 November to purchase the collection before administrators sell it to the highest bidder.

The collection is being sold to help pay off part of the ceramics firm's pension bill, inherited by the museum after Waterford Wedgwood Plc's collapse in 2009. The museum houses more than 80,000 historical pieces, works of art, photographs and archival material spanning Wedgwood's 250-year history, valued at £15m.

Art Fund director Stephen Deuchar praised the "exceptional" public support, which complements a £13m pledge from the Heritage Lottery Fund. JCB's donation, made through the Bamford Charitable Foundation, has been match-funded by a private charitable trust, contributing £200,000 to the appeal.

Approximately 8,000 former workers received payments from the Pension Protection Fund, and in 2011, a judge authorised the collection's sale to repay the remaining debt.

# Derbyshire Pub Dazzles with 53 Christmas Trees

A Victorian-era pub in Ripley, Derbyshire, has transformed into a festive wonderland with an impressive display of 53 Christmas trees adorning its premises.

The Angel pub, aptly named for the season, features trees of varying sizes, with the showstopper being a 22-foot (6.7-meter) specimen that cost owner Peter Clay over £1,000, including decorations. Adding to the spectacle is a permanent 9-foot (2.7-meter) golden angel positioned above the entrance, which has an unusual claim to fame – it previously graced the set of soap opera Crossroads.

Clay explained the tradition began three years ago during difficult economic times. "It started back in the middle of the recession. Everyone was depressed and saying it's doom and gloom," he said. "I'm a partly-sunny guy, not a partly-cloudy guy, so we thought we would do something to cheer everybody up."

The display has grown more elaborate each year, with customers invited to participate by hanging baubles on the trees. The distinctive building, constructed in 1888 for Queen Victoria's jubilee, is often mistaken for a chapel due to its architectural style.

# Welsh Government Takes "Formal Management Action" Over Failed Furniture Contract

Legal proceedings were brought by Triumph Furniture after it challenged a contract awarded to a rival competitor in a procurement dispute.

Top civil servant Sir Derek Jones has announced that "formal management action" has begun in relation to staff members involved in the controversial contract process. The contract in question was for furniture, fittings, planning and interior design services for three public bodies: the Welsh Government, the National Assembly, and the Higher Education Funding Council for Wales.

Sir Derek, the Welsh Government's permanent secretary, made his comments in a letter to the assembly's Public Accounts Committee. In the letter, he acknowledged the failings "centre around poor information management and a lack of oversight which, ultimately, weakened the position of the Welsh Government not only in terms of public perception of the robustness and transparency of the procurement process, but at the point where the Welsh Government was required to defend itself in subsequent litigation proceedings".

However, he stressed that "there is no evidence that anyone received personal gain from the procurement process".

The Welsh Government was alleged by Triumph Furniture to have breached EU procurement rules. Sir Derek previously told Assembly Members that compensation was paid following an arbitration process.

Keith Pelley has been named as the new chief executive of the European Tour, replacing George O'Grady who has held the position for over a decade.

The 51-year-old, president of Rogers Media in Canada for the last five years, will start his role this summer. An "honoured" Pelley said he wanted to ensure golf remained at the "forefront of the game" across the world.

O'Grady, 65, had been chief executive of the Tour, which runs the three leading men's professional golf circuits in Europe, since 2005.

David Williams, chairman of the European Tour, said: "Throughout the interview process, it was clear Keith has an unwavering passion for golf, as well as a strong grasp of the challenges and opportunities facing not only the European Tour, but the wider game of golf as a whole."

O'Grady, who will now take up a presidential role to represent the Tour through the 2016 Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro, said he would ensure a smooth transition. "I am certain Keith will bring a fresh and business-focused perspective to the Tour," he added.

# Rome Faces Drastic Water Rationing as Drought Crisis Deepens

Parts of Italy, including the Lazio region surrounding Rome, are grappling with a severe drought that has prompted emergency measures. Acea, the water utility serving the capital, has proposed implementing eight-hour daily water cuts that would affect approximately 1.5 million Rome residents.

The water company blames regional officials for preventing it from extracting supplies from Lake Bracciano, a nearby water source. Lazio authorities defended their decision, stating that lake levels have dropped dangerously low due to the ongoing drought, raising fears of an environmental catastrophe.

Health Minister Beatrice Lorenzin warned of serious consequences, stating: "An eventual suspension of the supply of water in Rome could seriously compromise the level of hygiene of all the accommodation structures, restaurants and public offices. But above all, it could seriously compromise the provision of essential health services."

While Acea maintains it has no alternative but to introduce rationing, both the water company and regional authorities have committed to continuing negotiations for a solution.

Italy is experiencing its third-driest spring in six decades, with two-thirds of farmland affected and agricultural losses estimated at €2 billion ($2.3 billion). Rome has endured two consecutive years of below-average rainfall.

The crisis has even reached the Vatican, which began shutting off its famous fountains on Tuesday as a conservation measure.

# Former Leeds Lord Mayor Neil Taggart Jailed for Child Sex Offences

A former Lord Mayor of Leeds has been jailed after admitting to a series of child sex offences that spanned six years.

Neil Taggart, 65, of Marlowe Court, Garforth, appeared at Leeds Crown Court where a judge declared his once high-standing reputation in the community now "lay in the gutter". He pleaded guilty in June to eight child sex offences committed between 2010 and 2016.

Taggart served as Leeds Lord Mayor in 2003 and was a Labour councillor for more than 30 years. He also held the position of West Yorkshire Police Authority chairman before being deselected by the Labour Party in October 2013 ahead of the 2014 election.

The former councillor was suspended by the party in October when allegations emerged and was subsequently dismissed after admitting to the offences.

A spokesman for the National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children (NSPCC) described Taggart as "just one of the growing number of offenders caught using the internet to access child abuse images."

"Every child in his sickening catalogue of images has suffered abuse in the real world," the spokesman said, calling for technology companies, government and law enforcement to commit resources to prevent such material being published.

Detective Superintendent Pat Twiggs of West Yorkshire Police condemned Taggart's actions, stating: "Offenders like Taggart, who seek out and distribute abusive images of children for the sexual gratification of themselves and others, play a significant role in the continuation of the appalling real-life abuse that these images capture."

Police confirmed the crimes involved a high volume of images, many of the most serious kind, accumulated over a significant period.

# Aberdeen FC Pushes Forward with Controversial Kingsford Stadium Plans

Aberdeen Football Club is pressing ahead with plans to build a new 20,000-capacity stadium and training facilities at Kingsford, near Westhill, close to the Aberdeen bypass.

The club insists the relocation is essential for securing a sustainable future, following years of planning difficulties with a previous proposal at Loirston, south of Aberdeen.

However, the development has sparked significant local opposition. The Say No To Kingsford Stadium campaign group is distributing information packs to residents, continuing their protest despite reporting online abuse last year. Aberdeen FC condemned any such harassment of campaigners.

Club chairman Stewart Milne has defended the choice, calling Kingsford "an ideal location for supporters."

The contentious project highlights the tension between the club's ambitions for modernisation and community concerns about the development's impact on the area.

# Irish Director of Rugby Kennedy Eyes Premiership Challenge

London Irish director of rugby Brian Kennedy is preparing his side for their return to the Premiership, starting with a season opener against Harlequins at Twickenham. The Exiles secured promotion from the Championship at the first attempt and are ready to face the challenges of top-flight rugby.

"We're happy to be back, but we know it's a huge, huge challenge ahead of us," Kennedy told BBC Sport.

Irish face a demanding opening month, with a trip to defending champions Exeter following the Harlequins match, plus Friday-night fixtures at Sale and Newcastle.

"Every game's difficult," Kennedy acknowledged. "We won't think about them individually until they come around."

Despite the tough schedule, Kennedy is delighted to be back in the Premiership. "We all love the Premiership. It's a league we thoroughly enjoy being in as a club," he said.

"We missed it and we did enjoy our time in the Championship, we felt we learnt a lot and built a lot of strong foundations down there. But, this is ultimately where we want to be."

Irish's squad will be strengthened by new signings including Samoa lock Teofilo Paulo and Fiji winger Napolioni Nalaga, who join for pre-season training.

"They're going to add experience, strength in depth and we're going to get competition for a few places now," Kennedy added.

# Hezbollah Vows Revenge After Samir Qantar Killed in Damascus Strike

Hezbollah has vowed that Israel will "pay the price" for the death of Samir Qantar, a former prisoner and senior operative killed in an alleged Israeli air strike in Damascus.

Speaking at Qantar's funeral in Beirut on Monday, Hezbollah executive council chief Hashem Safieddine issued a stark warning to Israel, declaring that the militant group would avenge the killing. Israel has welcomed Qantar's death but has not officially confirmed responsibility for the strike.

Qantar, who spent almost 30 years in Israeli prison for murder before being released in a 2008 prisoner exchange with Hezbollah, was killed along with eight others when missiles fired by Israeli jets reportedly hit a residential building in Damascus's Jaramana district on Saturday night, according to Hezbollah sources.

Thousands of mourners filled the streets of Ghobeiry, a southern Beirut suburb, on Monday, carrying Qantar's coffin draped in Hezbollah's distinctive yellow flag. Chants of "Death to Israel" echoed through the crowd as supporters paid their respects to the controversial figure.

In his funeral address, Mr Safieddine delivered a defiant message to Israel. "If the Israelis imagine that by targeting Samir Qantar they have closed an account, they are very wrong because they know and will know that they have opened accounts that are not closed with a treacherous missile," he declared.

Israeli cabinet minister Yuval Steinitz responded on Sunday by saying he was not sorry about Qantar's death, though he declined to comment on allegations of Israeli involvement in the strike.

Qantar, a Lebanese Druze, was just 16 years old when he participated in a deadly 1979 attack in the Israeli coastal town of Nahariya alongside three other members of the Palestine Liberation Front. The raid resulted in the deaths of two policemen, a civilian man, and his four-year-old daughter. Tragically, a two-year-old girl also died when her mother accidentally smothered her while trying to keep her quiet as they hid in a cupboard.

Nearly three decades later, Hezbollah secured Qantar's release in exchange for the bodies of two Israeli soldiers captured in 2006. Upon his return to Lebanon, he is believed to have joined Hezbollah's armed wing.

While Hezbollah has not publicly disclosed Qantar's role in Syria, where thousands of its fighters support government forces, his brother wrote in the Lebanese newspaper al-Akhbar that Qantar had been involved in "resistance" activities against Israel's occupation of the Syrian Golan Heights since his release. He claimed Israel had attempted to assassinate him six times previously.

The United States identified Qantar as one of Hezbollah's "most visible and popular spokesmen" who had "played an operational role, with the assistance of Iran and Syria, in building up Hezbollah's terrorist infrastructure in the Golan Heights."

Israel has conducted several air strikes inside Syria since 2011. In January, a suspected Israeli strike in the Syrian Golan Heights killed six Hezbollah fighters, including the son of the group's late military chief Imad Mughniyeh, and an Iranian Revolutionary Guards general.

**Burton Albion Sign Leeds Midfielder on Permanent Deal**

Burton Albion have completed the permanent signing of the 27-year-old midfielder who impressed during his loan spell last season.

The Crewe academy graduate initially joined Albion in January, making 19 appearances and scoring once as the club secured their survival.

Since joining Leeds in 2013, he has amassed over 100 appearances for the Yorkshire club.

Manager Nigel Clough praised his new signing: "He's quiet and unassuming, he's maturing into his role, knows what he's good at, knows his limitations and plays accordingly."

Australia batter Meg Lanning has withdrawn from the inaugural Women's Cricket Super League due to injury concerns.

The 24-year-old was scheduled to represent Surrey Stars but will instead remain in Australia to focus on her rehabilitation programme.

"The tournament concept and growth of women's cricket across the globe is fantastic and I would have loved to have taken part," Lanning said.

The Super League, featuring six teams competing in 15 Twenty20 matches in a round-robin format, begins on 30 July.

Lanning's withdrawal follows England wicketkeeper Sarah Taylor's decision not to play for Lancashire Thunder this year, as she takes an indefinite break from cricket to address anxiety issues.

# Swansea Council Leader David Phillips Steps Down After Decade in Charge

David Phillips has announced his resignation as leader of Swansea Council after 10 years at the helm of the Labour group.

Mr Phillips said the decision was made to focus on building Swansea's regional and national profile, although details of his new role are not yet known. It comes a week after he was told to expect a leadership challenge after sacking two cabinet members in a reshuffle, but he would not comment on whether his departure was linked.

The Labour group has been in power at the authority for the last two years. The selection process to find a new leader begins on Monday.

Speaking about his decision, Mr Phillips said from the back benches he will continue to give his "complete support to the new cabinet and the group as we work to continue to deliver on our manifesto commitments for the good of the people of Swansea and the wider region".

Labour group chairman Robert Francis Davies praised the outgoing leader, saying: "David Phillips has made an enormous contribution to Swansea and to Labour and will continue to do so in the future. We want to keep his talents working for our city."

# Climber Dies from Natural Causes on Snowdonia Mountain

A 52-year-old man from Nottingham has died from natural causes while climbing in Snowdonia.

Neil Parnell fell from Bristley Ridge, between Tryfan and Glyder Fach, at approximately 15:00 GMT on Saturday.

His body was airlifted to Ysbyty Gwynedd, where he was pronounced dead.

A post-mortem examination confirmed he died from natural causes, and no inquest will be held.

# Essex Cruise to Victory as Westley and Pettini Dominate Warwickshire

Essex secured a comprehensive victory over Warwickshire in their One-Day Cup encounter, with Tom Westley and Mark Pettini delivering match-winning performances at Chelmsford.

The pair put on 191 for the first wicket before Westley was trapped lbw by spinner Jeetan Patel for 108. Pettini struck 126, with 10 fours and two sixes, as Essex piled up 320-5.

Warwickshire and former England batsman Jonathan Trott made 51, but he was removed by Westley (2-26) as the visitors were bowled out for 168. Left-armer Reece Topley also shone with the ball for the hosts claiming 4-29.

Essex now top the early Group B table with two wins and a no result, while Warwickshire are bottom with two defeats and a washed out game.

Essex opener Tom Westley reflected: "I wouldn't say it was a difficult wicket but we had to work hard for the runs so to put on 191 with Mark for the first wicket was very rewarding. That set the platform for others to come in and finish the job off."

Warwickshire director of cricket Dougie Brown admitted: "Essex played very well but was still a disappointing result, more so because we failed to reach the standards we set ourselves."

**FA Cup Third Round: Team News and Fourth Round Draw**

Ashley Eastham stands ready to deputise for Pond should fitness concerns prevent his participation, with new signing Joe Maguire poised for a potential debut following his transfer from Liverpool.

Bristol City's defensive options improve as Hordur Magnusson nears recovery from hamstring problems. Midfielders Gary O'Neil and Callum O'Dowda are also pushing for returns to the starting lineup.

However, the Robins remain without Korey Smith and Adam Matthews, sidelined with hamstring and calf injuries respectively.

The victors will face either Burnley or Sunderland away in the fourth round, with both Premier League sides awaiting their own third-round outcome.

# Wolves striker Nouha Dicko faces extended layoff after minor knee surgery

Wolverhampton Wanderers striker Nouha Dicko will miss an additional three weeks of training after undergoing minor knee surgery, further delaying his return from a serious injury that has sidelined him for nearly an entire season.

The France-born 24-year-old has been absent for almost the whole of the 2015-16 campaign after suffering an injury during Wolves' 2-1 home victory over Charlton in late August. The Championship club initially ruled Dicko out for nine months, but the recent surgical procedure will extend his rehabilitation period.

Wolves had originally hoped the striker would be fit to start the new season, which begins with a trip to his former club Rotherham United on 6 August. However, those plans now appear in jeopardy following the latest setback.

Wolves head of medical Phil Hayward explained the situation to the Express & Star: "He's undergone some minor surgery to have a staple taken from his knee. It's a very small, minor procedure. It's quite common with surgery. Probably half of people who have surgery have the staple taken out."

Hayward emphasised the decision was made strategically: "We thought it best to do it now rather than delay it and potentially do it during the season. It'll be a case of easing him back in August. It's not a big issue."

He added: "If he's going to be out for a few weeks we're better off doing it now and missing a bit of pre-season, rather than in September or October and missing four or five games."

The news comes amid ongoing uncertainty about the club's ownership. Wolves could be in new hands by the start of next season, as talks progress to end Steve Morgan's ownership of the club.

More than one interested party is currently in discussions with Morgan, who put Wolves up for sale last September. Sources indicate talks are proceeding constructively, with the club finishing 14th in the Championship and Morgan reportedly reluctant to spend additional money on new players.

Wolves, along with West Midlands neighbours Aston Villa and West Bromwich Albion, have been the subject of reported Chinese ownership interest.

The asking price is understood to be in the region of £50m. Morgan would take a substantial financial hit on the deal, having invested £30m initially and approximately another £75m on new players, upgrading the training facility to Category 1 Academy status and developing a new stand at Molineux.

The club owns the Molineux stadium and all assets, leasing the ground from the council on a 999-year lease at a peppercorn rent, which should make any potential sale relatively straightforward once agreement is reached.

Wrexham vice-captain Michael Carrington has signed a new one-year contract with the National League club.

The 29-year-old former Crewe and Bury player joined Wrexham in September 2013 and has been a key figure for the Welsh side.

Manager Dean Keates confirmed the club has also reached an agreement with midfielder Paul Rutherford for next season.

Keates revealed negotiations continue with top-scorer John Rooney, who scored twice as a substitute in Saturday's 3-1 victory over Guiseley. Rooney is just one start away from automatically triggering a new contract clause.

# Welsh Boxing Champion Rachael Buckland Awakes from Coma Ahead of Schedule

A Welsh boxing champion is showing remarkable signs of recovery after awakening from an induced coma two months earlier than doctors expected.

Rachael Buckland, 25, suffered life-threatening injuries in October when she fell at her Cardiff home, fracturing her skull and causing a bleed on the brain. The mother of two, who is married to Celtic boxing champion Mitchell Buckland, required emergency surgery at Cardiff's University Hospital of Wales.

During the operation, surgeons removed a piece of bone and a damaged section of her brain. Medical professionals initially predicted she would remain in a coma until the new year.

However, her former coach Tony Borg announced the encouraging news that Mrs Buckland is now awake and able to recognise people around her. "This is a really positive sign and we are naturally delighted," he said. "She's definitely showing that fighting spirit."

The former bantamweight champion, originally from Magor in Monmouthshire, still faces a lengthy recovery journey. Mr Borg, who also coaches Welsh world featherweight boxing champion Lee Selby, emphasized that whilst progress is encouraging, there remains considerable work ahead.

The boxing community has rallied around the family, with friends organizing fundraising events. So far, approximately £6,500 has been raised to support Mrs Buckland's family during this difficult time. She works as a chef at a Newport pub when not training.

# Rare 1962 Beatles Acetate Disc Sells for Record Price at Auction

A rare 10-inch acetate disc featuring early Beatles recordings has sold for an undisclosed sum at a Warrington auction, with Omega Auctions expressing they were "nicely surprised" by the final price paid by a Manchester collector.

The 78 RPM record, dating from 1962, contains recordings of "Till There Was You" and "Hello Little Girl" and has been described by Beatles historian Mark Lewisohn as "a Holy Grail item" and one of the "rarest and most collectable of all Beatles records."

The disc was cut at the HMV store in Oxford Street, London, before the Beatles achieved national chart success. It bears handwriting from the band's manager, Brian Epstein, though contains notable misspellings – labelling the tracks as "'Til There Was You" and "Hullo Little Girl." The recordings were credited to "Paul McCartney & The Beatles" and "John Lennon & The Beatles" respectively.

Created as part of Epstein's effort to secure a recording contract, the acetate was presented to George Martin, who would later become the Beatles' producer, at EMI record label. Martin, who died in March 2016, eventually returned the disc to Epstein.

The record's owner, Les Maguire, 74, was keyboardist for fellow Liverpool band Gerry and the Pacemakers. He received the disc as a gift from Epstein in 1963 and stored it in his Formby loft for over 50 years, wrapped in paper.

Maguire called it "a special piece" but decided to sell, giving the proceeds to his granddaughter to help purchase a house after completing her accountancy exams. "It's no good to me," he explained.

The sale represents a significant moment in Beatles memorabilia collecting history.

# Swan Shot with Pellet Gun Had to Be Put Down

A swan discovered with severe injuries at Monks Pond, between Glasbury and Painscastle in Hay-on-Wye, has been put down after veterinary examination.

The bird was found by a member of the public at approximately 11:00 GMT on Wednesday and immediately taken to veterinary care. However, the extent of its injuries was so severe that the swan had to be euthanized.

Dyfed-Powys Police have confirmed the swan was shot with a pellet gun. Sergeant Craig Morgan condemned the incident as "absolutely appalling."

Officers in Hay-on-Wye are conducting enquiries into the attack. Sgt Morgan has urged anyone with information about those responsible to come forward immediately.

# Wrexham Captain Corry Evans Among Nine Players Released

Wrexham have announced that captain Corry Evans will leave the club along with eight other players following the end of the season.

Evans, 21, was appointed captain in November and has made over 100 appearances for his hometown club.

Iffy Allen, Khaellem Bailey-Nichols, Anthony Barry, Shwan Jalal, Izale McLeod, Callum Powell, Martin Riley, and Jordan White will also depart the Racecourse Ground.

Additionally, Curtis Tilt, Hamza Bencherif, and John Rooney have all requested transfers after spending time on loan elsewhere this season. Tilt joined Forest Green Rovers, Bencherif linked up with former manager Gary Mills at York City, while Rooney moved to Guiseley.

The Dragons are hoping to extend defender James Jennings' stay after his loan from Cheltenham Town.

# Young Zambian Footballer Vows to Return After Tragic Accident

**Chingola, Zambia** - While his teammates competed in the Africa Cup of Nations in Equatorial Guinea, promising young Zambian midfielder Changwe Kalale lay in a hospital bed, battling injuries that doctors say may end his football career before it truly began.

The 17-year-old was involved in a devastating road accident on December 14 while traveling to Lusaka to join Zambia's pre-Nations Cup training camp. Kalale, along with teammates Nyambe Mulenga and Satchmo Chakawa, was a passenger in a minibus that collided head-on with another vehicle.

The accident claimed four lives and left eight others injured, with Kalale suffering the most severe consequences. A spinal injury has left him with limited movement from the waist down, and medical professionals have delivered a crushing prognosis: he may never walk again, let alone play professional football.

Despite the grim outlook, Kalale remains defiant and determined. Speaking exclusively to BBC Sport from his bed at Nchanga South Hospital in Chingola, the young midfielder refused to accept that his career is over.

"I can't give up on football just because of that accident," Kalale said. "After the accident, I wasn't able to move. All I could do is sleep on the bed. But I'll be back, I know I will play football again. It's a matter of time."

The timing of the accident was particularly cruel for the talented teenager, who was on the verge of potentially representing his country at a major tournament. Having earned his first senior international cap in a friendly against Ivory Coast in October, Kalale was widely regarded as one of Zambia's brightest young prospects.

"It has been a very painful experience for me especially because my career was on the rise," he reflected. "I'm sure I'd have played at the Africa Cup of Nations but the accident ruined all my plans."

The incident has reignited discussions about the welfare of players injured while on national duty. Although the Football Association of Zambia has acknowledged the situation, they have indicated limited capacity to provide comprehensive support.

However, Kalale's father, Bernard, has refused to assign blame for the tragedy. "I have three sons who play football and what happened to Changwe cannot make me tell them to stop playing football - it was an accident and it could have happened to anyone," he said.

Bernard added that the family draws strength from their son's survival. "There was a period when my son was critical and we never thought he would come back to life in the manner he has. As a family, we are really grateful for all the support we are receiving and we take a lot of courage and confidence that our son will play football again."

Kalale now faces months of intensive physiotherapy and rehabilitation, motivated by the realization that he "could be dead or completely paralysed." His determination to return to the sport he loves serves as an inspiration to many who face similar challenges.

# Friends of Snibston Group Seeks Judicial Review Over Museum Closure

A group campaigning to save Snibston Discovery Museum has applied for a judicial review of Leicestershire County Council's decision to close the attraction.

The county council decided in January to replace the Snibston Discovery Museum with a smaller attraction to save money. A plan by the Friends of Snibston to run the current museum as a charitable trust was dismissed by the authority.

The council said it followed proper processes. The group intends to take legal action on grounds including the council's consultation on the museum's future being "flawed".

Brian Vollar, chair of Friends of Snibston, said: "We think we have a strong case, else we wouldn't have proceeded along with this plan. We have given plenty of indication of our intention to follow this plan and plenty of opportunity for the council to be more accommodating in following the people's wishes and not going ahead with the decision to close."

He said they would be informed in six weeks whether permission will be given for a review.

A spokesman for Leicestershire County Council said: "The council maintains that proper processes were followed to arrive at the conclusions reached by the cabinet. We will study the application in detail and assess the implications for the council."

Snibston Discovery Museum is focused on industry and design but also has a theatre and large country park.

# Cavendish to Support Boasson Hagen in Paris-Roubaix Return

Mark Cavendish will make his return to Paris-Roubaix on Sunday, riding in support of Norwegian teammate Edvald Boasson Hagen in cycling's grueling one-day classic.

The Manxman has attempted the 'Queen of the Classics' only once, when he failed to finish in 2011. The sprinter, 30, said: "I hope to get a bit deeper into the race than last time and help Edvald later on."

Cavendish has won 26 Tour de France stages and the Milan-San Remo 'monument' in 2009. However, the 257.5km route across northern France, nicknamed the 'Hell of the North', is famous for its cobbled sections that don't suit the British sprinter's strengths.

Switzerland's Fabian Cancellara, who won Paris-Roubaix in 2006, 2010 and 2013, and Slovakian world champion Peter Sagan - winner of the Tour of Flanders last Sunday - are the favourites.

Defending champion John Degenkolb, from Germany, is absent as he continues his recovery after being hit by a car while training in Spain in January.

Britain's Luke Rowe, who finished fifth in the Tour of Flanders, and Ian Stannard will lead Team Sky's challenge.

The 2011 world champion Cavendish said: "We've come to Roubaix and we've got no pressure. We're not the big favourites but definitely we can be in the mix at the end."

Cavendish, who won the Tour of Qatar for the second time in February, is focusing on this year's Tour de France and the Rio Olympics.

# Teenager Leah Kerry Dies After Taking New Psychoactive Substances

A 15-year-old schoolgirl from Salisbury has died after taking new psychoactive substances (NPS), prompting her family to issue an urgent warning about the dangers of so-called "legal highs."

Leah Kerry was found unconscious at an address in Newton Abbot, Devon, and died in hospital on 16 July. Her family described her as "a courageous and confident young woman" who was aware of the risks but "thought she was invincible."

In a heartfelt statement released through Devon and Cornwall Police, the family said: "Leah lit up any room she walked into with her incredible personality, sense of humour, striking looks and demeanour. Those who know her will ache to hear the words 'You allriiight' one last time."

The family emphasized that despite knowing the dangers of drugs, Leah believed she was invulnerable. "Sadly, despite being well aware of the risks, she thought she was invincible and she rolled the dice and has paid the ultimate price," they said.

Her relatives are calling on the government to prioritize the dangers of psychoactive substances following the 2017 Drugs Strategy, urging other young people to avoid dangerous NPS tablets.

Jacob Khanlarian, 20, from Newton Abbot, has been charged with intent to supply drugs in connection with the incident and will appear before Exeter Crown Court on 10 August.

# Mysterious Foam on Welsh Beaches Identified as Harmless Algae

Natural Resources Wales has confirmed that mysterious foam appearing on several Pembrokeshire beaches is naturally occurring algae, not pollution. The algae species, Phaeocystis and Chaetocerus, commonly deceive beachgoers due to their oily appearance and seaweed-like odour.

Thriving in warm weather conditions, the algae has been identified at Barafundle, Cwm-yr-Eglwys, Freshwater East, Lydstep, Newgale, and Tenby beaches. Officials anticipate additional sightings as temperatures remain elevated throughout the region.

# Coldplay's New Album Misses Top Spot Despite Strong Sales

Coldplay's latest album "A Head Full Of Dreams" has become the band's first studio album not to debut at number one in the UK charts, despite impressive sales of 236,000 copies in its opening week.

The British rock band's previous releases had consistently topped the charts, with 2014's "Ghost Stories" debuting with 168,000 sales and 2011's "Mylo Xyloto" selling 208,000 copies in its first week.

In the singles chart, Bieber secured a second consecutive week at number one with "Love Yourself," having replaced his own song the previous week. Sigala's "Sweet Lovin'" was the highest new entry at three, while Adele's "Hello" held fourth place.

The festive season influenced both charts, with Mariah Carey's "All I Want For Christmas Is You" climbing to 13, The Pogues' "Fairytale Of New York" at 20, and Wham's "Last Christmas" reaching 27.

# From Reality TV to Hampshire: Ian Holland's Unique Journey to County Cricket

Ian Holland's path to professional cricket with Hampshire reads like something from a screenplay, beginning with an Australian reality television show and culminating in a promising county cricket career in England.

The 26-year-old all-rounder, born in the United States but holding a British passport through his English father, credits former Australian Test captain Allan Border for launching his professional career. In 2012, Holland won Cricket Superstar, a Foxtel television series that saw him triumph over 14 other finalists selected through national trials.

"It was one of those unique opportunities that popped up," Holland told BBC Radio Solent. "I went into it without any expectations and came out with an opportunity. It was a chance to fast-track myself at that point of my career and it got me a foot in the door of the Australian system."

The prize was a rookie contract with Victoria, Australia's state side. The show featured Border as chief judge, with former wicket-keeper Graham Manou as mentor and guest appearances from cricket legends Matthew Hayden and Ricky Ponting.

"It was a strange experience watching yourself back on television," Holland admitted. "There were a few challenges that looked good on camera, but it was Allan Border's involvement that gave it the credibility for me."

However, despite his television success, opportunities at Victoria proved limited. Holland eventually looked to the Northern Hemisphere, spending two years playing for Fleetwood Cricket Club in the Northern League before his Hampshire connection materialised.

"Dimitri Mascarenhas is the connection to Hampshire from the time he moved back to Melbourne," explained the right-hand batsman and medium-pace bowler. "I played some second-team cricket here last season and then the first XI chances have come this year."

Holland's impressive figures of 4-16 and 2-23 against Somerset in the County Championship this week have built on earlier limited-overs and four-day appearances this campaign.

"It's been a really great transition for me," Holland revealed. "I'm really enjoying my cricket here and it's just a great place to play. My goal is to play here for the rest of my career."

Ian Holland was talking to BBC Radio Solent's Kevan James.

# Brothers Jailed for Grooming and Sexually Assaulting Nine Teenage Girls

Two brothers who exploited their positions working in convenience stores to groom and sexually assault nine vulnerable teenage girls have been jailed for a combined total of 41 years.

Ilvarasan Rajenthiram, 26, of Wallasey Village, Wirral, was sentenced to 22 and a half years in prison, while his brother Vinothan Rajenthiram, 27, of Wigan, received 18 and a half years. The pair were found guilty of a total of 30 charges spanning more than five years.

Sentencing them at Liverpool Crown Court, Judge Norman Wright said "both abused their position in the shops to target teenage girls". The grooming happened at convenience stores the brothers worked in at Birkenhead, Walton and Garston between 2010 and January 2016.

## Pattern of Grooming

Judge Wright said they gave the 14 and 15-year-old girls free sweets and mobile phone top-ups, as well as serving them cigarettes, "to win their trust and confidence". The pair, known to victims as Ara and Vino, then invited them to go for drives, listen to music and "chill out".

"The final step was to take them back to unoccupied flats and ply them with alcohol," the judge said. Judge Wright added that it was all about the brothers' "sexual gratification".

Detective Superintendent Dave Brunskill described the pair as "calculating sexual predators who went to extraordinary lengths to groom their victims". He said: "In most cases, they gained the trust of the young girls then took the relationship further by coercing the girls to take part in sexual activity after plying them with alcohol.

"Victims mistakenly believed that these men genuinely had feelings for them and they didn't realise that they were being groomed and sexually exploited."

## Impact on Victims

In a statement to court, one of the victims said the experience had "ruined my life". She said she "trusted him to be a good person" and thought they had "something special".

"I had not done anything wrong," she said. "I was just a vulnerable, naive child who should have been safe in his company."

The mother of another victim said their sentences "will never justify the damage they have caused my daughter and all the others involved".

"The fact that those men pleaded not guilty sickened me and proves that they feel no guilt, shame or remorse. They have no conscience in my eyes," she added.

Ilvarasan was found guilty of 15 counts of sexual activity with a child, three counts of sexual assault and two counts of perverting the course of justice. Vinothan was convicted of four counts of sexual assault, one rape, four counts of sexual activity with a child and one count of perverting the course of justice.

The pair were ordered to sign the Sex Offenders Register for life.

# County Antrim Shield: Linfield Thrash Cliftonville 3-0 as Holders Ballymena Crash Out

Linfield eased into the next round of the County Antrim Shield with a commanding 3-0 victory over Cliftonville at Windsor Park on Tuesday night.

# Wales Focus on Moldova Despite Hull City's Interest in Coleman

The Football Association of Wales (FAW) has firmly rejected Hull City's approach to speak with manager Chris Coleman, as the national team remains concentrated on their upcoming World Cup qualifier against Moldova.

FAW chief executive Jonathan Ford and the organization stood behind their 46-year-old manager, who recently led Wales to a historic semi-final appearance at Euro 2016. Coleman had signed a new two-year contract with the FAW just a month before the tournament.

# London Shooting: Gang-Related Murder Case of Mistaken Identity, Police Say

A 27-year-old man, identified in reports as Oliver Tetlow, has been pronounced dead following a shooting in Harlesden on Wednesday night.

Detective Chief Inspector Mark Lawson confirmed the killing is being investigated as gang-related, revealing the victim was shot multiple times with what appeared to be an automatic weapon.

DCI Lawson acknowledged that details of the murder are "circulating" on social media and urged anyone with information to contact authorities.

The victim's family has been notified, though formal identification will only occur following a post-mortem examination.

Investigators continue to appeal for witnesses to come forward as they work to piece together the circumstances of this fatal shooting.

**Murtagh Returns as Ireland Name Squad for England ODI**

Tim Murtagh has been included in Ireland's 14-man squad for the one-day international against England at Malahide on 8 May after recovering from the foot injury that ruled him out of the World Cup.

**Squad:** William Porterfield (captain), Andrew Balbirnie, Alex Cusack, George Dockrell, Ed Joyce, Andrew McBrine, John Mooney, Tim Murtagh, Kevin O'Brien, Niall O'Brien, Paul Stirling, Stuart Thompson, Gary Wilson, Craig Young.

# Brighton seafront pool plans spark concerns over impact on Saltdean Lido

Plans for a new outdoor swimming pool on Brighton's seafront have drawn criticism from an MP and operators of a nearby historic lido, who warn the proximity of the two facilities could harm both businesses.

The proposed 50-metre pool would be built on a derelict council-owned site on Madeira Drive, just 3.9 miles from Saltdean Lido, a 1930s facility currently undergoing restoration and scheduled to open next year.

Brighton Kemptown MP Simon Kirby questioned the wisdom of having two outdoor pools so close together. "There is only a certain demand, and I'm not sure having two outdoor pools within three miles of each other is a very sensible way forward," he said.

Rebecca Crook from Saltdean Lido echoed these concerns, stating that "two outdoor swimming pools within a four-mile radius is most unusual and certainly will impact on both businesses." She also criticised what she described as a "lack of joined-up thinking."

However, developers behind the new pool insist the facilities would serve different purposes. Rod Hart from Swimmergy, one of three companies involved in the project, said the 50m pool would focus primarily on training rather than general swimming, targeting triathletes and swimming squads from around the world.

Brighton and Hove Council defended the plans, saying the new pool would provide "excellence and broad appeal" and become a hub for swimming and sport-related businesses. The facility would be marketed for triathlons and offer escorted sea swims, lifeguard training, and leisure swimming.

Councillor Geoffrey Bowden, chairman of the economic development and culture committee, emphasised that Saltdean Lido was "a very different facility" with its own unique offering. His committee will decide on Thursday whether to grant landlord's consent for the project.

# Three People Injured in Bradford Shooting Incident

Armed police responded to a shooting at a property on Parkway in Bradford during the early hours of Saturday morning at approximately 01:00 BST.

Three people were injured in the incident – two men aged 22 and 41, and a 38-year-old woman. All three victims required hospital treatment but have since been discharged.

# Putin 'Probably Approved' Litvinenko Murder, UK Inquiry Finds

The assassination of former Russian spy Alexander Litvinenko in London was probably approved by President Vladimir Putin himself, according to a landmark British public inquiry released today.

"Taking full account of all the evidence and analysis available to me, I find that the FSB operation to kill Litvinenko was probably approved by Mr Patrushev and also by President Putin," wrote Sir Robert Owen, who led the inquiry. This is the most significant statement to come out of the report, says the BBC's Richard Galpin.

Nikolai Patrushev was head of Russia's main intelligence agency, FSB, at the time of the murder and very close to Mr Putin.

Mr Litvinenko died from acute radiation syndrome on 23 November 2006, three weeks after drinking tea containing polonium-210 in a hotel bar in central London's Mayfair, the inquiry found.

The report identified two Russian men, Andrei Lugovoi and Dmitry Kovtun, as the perpetrators. For many years, they have been the two chief suspects. Mr Lugovoi had been in the FSB and the federal protection service, and continued to have strong links to the FSB.

Sir Robert said there was a strong probability that Mr Lugovoi poisoned Mr Litvinenko under the direction of Moscow's FSB intelligence service. Mr Kovtun was also acting under FSB direction, possibly indirectly through Mr Lugovoi but probably to his knowledge.

The Russian pair had tried to poison Mr Litvinenko almost a month earlier at a London office of multinational security company, Erinys, the report said. They knew they were using a deadly poison, but did not know precisely which chemical, it went on.

Both deny killing Mr Litvinenko. They are wanted in the UK for questioning, but Russia has refused to extradite them.

The use of polonium-210 was "at the very least a strong indicator of state involvement" as it had to be made in a nuclear reactor, the report said.

Possible motives were Mr Litvinenko's work for British intelligence agencies, his criticism of Mr Putin and the FSB and his association with other Russian dissidents, the report said. There was "undoubtedly a personal dimension to the antagonism" between Mr Putin and Mr Litvinenko, Sir Robert said.

The inquiry heard evidence that Mr Litvinenko may have been consigned to a slow death from radiation to "send a message".

# Lewes Parking Meters Targeted in Latest Vandalism Attack

Parking meters in Lewes have been targeted in the latest of a series of vandalism attacks that have plagued the Sussex town for nearly a decade.

In the most recent incident, four meters were attacked with fireworks while paint was daubed on a fifth machine. A witness reported seeing a man running towards the town centre following an explosion heard in Friars Walk at 22:00 BST on Sunday, according to Sussex Police.

The attacks caused approximately £4,500 worth of damage, affecting machines in Phoenix Causeway car park, Friars Walk, Garden Street and Southover Road.

This continues a disturbing pattern of vandalism. A previous attack in October 2012 resulted in £2,900 of damage to two pay-and-display machines.

The most serious spate occurred in 2011, when vandals carried out 15 attacks on 14 parking meters between September and November, causing over £20,000 in damage.

Police say similar incidents have been reported annually since on-street parking charges were introduced in 2004.

# Northern Ireland to Host Major Aviation Conference Routes Europe 2017

Belfast is set to welcome approximately 1,200 delegates when it hosts Routes Europe in early 2017, organisers have announced. The prestigious annual conference brings together airports and tourism authorities from across the continent.

Northern Ireland Enterprise Minister Arlene Foster emphasized the significance of securing the event. "It is not just any old conference," she said. "Any city which has held it comes out the other side with more routes."

The conference comes at a crucial time for Northern Ireland's three airports, which have struggled to open new markets while competing with the rapid growth of Dublin Airport. Airlines have cited air passenger duty (APD) as a barrier to establishing new routes, particularly to destinations like Germany.

Mrs Foster currently opposes devolving complete APD control to Stormont, as any tax cut would require the executive to reimburse the Treasury for lost revenue—estimated at £55 million annually. However, she supports establishing an air route development fund to attract specific airlines and routes. "I am hoping that will come about soon," she stated.

Both Belfast International and George Best Belfast City airports have welcomed the news. Following this year's event in Aberdeen and next year's conference in Krakow, the Belfast gathering will take place at the newly revamped Waterfront Hall.

# Angolan Activists Face Trial for Discussing Book on Nonviolent Resistance

A group of Angolan activists, including prominent rapper and activist Luaty Beirao, are facing trial after being arrested in June for participating in a book club discussion about nonviolent resistance.

The activists, who belong to a youth movement critical of the government, were detained while preparing to discuss Gene Sharp's 1993 book "From Dictatorship to Democracy: A Conceptual Framework for Liberation." The book, which has become a handbook for democratic movements worldwide, outlines strategies for peaceful resistance against authoritarian regimes.

Mr. Beirao, who performs under the stage name Ikonoklasta, has been a vocal critic of Angola's government, advocating for more equitable distribution of the country's substantial oil wealth. He recently ended a five-week hunger strike while in detention.

The arrests have sparked international concern, with protests erupting in Portugal and widespread condemnation from human rights organizations. Zenaida Machado of Human Rights Watch called on Angolan judges to "show independence and not permit this trial to be used as an instrument to silence the government's critics."

Angola's deputy state prosecutor defended the detentions, claiming the activists were planning an uprising among students and workers "with incalculable consequences." If convicted, the group faces up to 12 years in prison.

The detained activists had previously organized demonstrations calling for the resignation of President Jose Eduardo dos Santos, who has ruled Angola for 36 years. Despite Angola being Africa's second-largest oil producer and experiencing significant economic growth since the civil war ended in 2002, critics argue that the nation's wealth has only enriched a small elite while the majority of citizens remain impoverished.

The case highlights ongoing tensions between civil society and the government in Angola.

# Trial Opens for Two Men Accused in Alan Kurdi's Death

The trial has begun in Turkey for two Syrian nationals accused in connection with the death of three-year-old Alan Kurdi, whose photograph lying lifeless on a Turkish beach became a defining image of the 2015 refugee crisis.

Mufawaka Alabash and Asem Alfrhad are being tried in Bodrum, the same seaside city where Alan's body washed ashore. The men face up to 35 years in prison each if convicted on charges of human smuggling and causing deaths "through deliberate negligence."

Both defendants pleaded not guilty at Thursday's hearing, which has reportedly concluded. Their next court appearance is scheduled for early March, and they will remain in custody until then.

Alan, along with his five-year-old brother Galib and mother Rihan, drowned when their overcrowded boat capsized during an attempted crossing to the Greek island of Kos. Alan's father, Abdullah, was the sole family survivor and is believed to be living outside Turkey.

The tragic photograph of Alan sparked global outrage and brought unprecedented attention to the Syrian refugee crisis.

# Leicester Tigers Sign Wales Sevens Star Owen Jenkins and Australia's Nick Malouf

Leicester Tigers have bolstered their backline with the signings of Wales Sevens international Owen Jenkins and Australia Sevens player Nick Malouf.

Back Malouf, 24, made his international Sevens debut in 2012 and played every game of the 2013 and 2014 World Series, as well as last year's Olympic Games.

# WWI Hero's Bronze Statue Unveiled in Middlesbrough

A bronze statue honoring Private Tom Dresser, a World War I hero from Middlesbrough, has been unveiled at the town's Dorman Museum following a remarkable fundraising effort by his family.

Pte Dresser displayed exceptional courage during the 1917 Battle of Arras in Northern France, running through No Man's Land to deliver two crucial messages despite being shot. He survived his wounds and lived until 1982, reaching the age of 90.

# Row the Rock Challenge Postponed Due to Rough Seas

A crew of 17 friends comprising the Row the Rock Challenge team has been forced to postpone their attempt to circumnavigate the Isle of Man due to adverse weather conditions.

The team had planned to depart from Peel earlier but was prevented by strong winds creating waves too dangerous for their vessel to safely navigate during the 90-mile round trip.

# Facebook Reports Soaring Mobile Ad Revenue as Zuckerberg Seeks New Share Structure

Facebook has announced stellar first-quarter results that significantly exceeded Wall Street expectations, with advertising revenues climbing to $5.2 billion and mobile advertising now accounting for more than 80% of the company's total ad revenue.

The social media giant reported total sales of $5.4 billion for the quarter, representing a substantial increase from $3.5 billion during the same period last year. Following the announcement, Facebook shares surged more than 9% in after-hours trading, demonstrating investor confidence in the company's continued growth trajectory.

## Mobile Strategy Pays Dividends

Facebook's strategic emphasis on mobile advertising has proven remarkably successful, with mobile now generating 82% of the company's advertising revenues for the first quarter of 2016, up from 73% during the corresponding quarter in 2015. This growth comes despite earlier investor concerns about the company's ability to transition effectively to mobile platforms.

The company's focus on live video has attracted new advertisers to the platform, while sales from existing services have also experienced robust growth. Total monthly active users (MAU) increased 15% year-over-year to reach 1.65 billion, surpassing analyst predictions. Facebook's impressive performance stands in stark contrast to recent struggles elsewhere in the technology sector, including disappointing results from Apple and ongoing challenges at Twitter. # Bushcricket Breaks Records with Testicles 14% of Body Weight

Scientists have discovered that a species of bushcricket possesses the largest testicles in relation to body weight ever recorded in the animal kingdom, according to a new study published in Biology Letters.

The species Platycleis affinis has testicles that make up approximately 14% of its body weight – equivalent to a human male having testicles weighing five kilograms (11 pounds) each. This surpasses the previous record holder, a fruit fly species called Drosophila bifurca, whose testicle-to-body weight ratio was recorded at 10.6%.

However, the research team led by Dr Karim Vahed of the University of Derby has uncovered a surprising twist that challenges long-held assumptions about the purpose of large testicles in the animal kingdom.

## Mating Strategy Over Sperm Competition

When studying the mating strategies of these bushcrickets, also known as katydids, researchers found that males with bigger testicles actually release only small amounts of sperm at each mating encounter. This discovery suggests that the oversized reproductive organs are designed for mating with many different females rather than producing competitive volumes of sperm for individual encounters.

"Males with bigger testicles are actually producing smaller amounts of ejaculate," Dr Vahed told BBC News. "This very much favours the alternative hypothesis: that it's about the number of different females the male can fertilise, rather than getting a greater success per female."

## Challenging Established Theory

Significant research across the animal kingdom has previously shown that male testicle size correlates with the degree of promiscuity within a species. The more partners a female has, the larger the male's testicles tend to be.

The traditional assumption has been that larger testicles produce more sperm for a "numbers game" within the female reproductive system, where the male providing the highest amount of sperm has a better chance of fathering offspring. Many experiments in vertebrate species, including our closest primate relatives, have supported this theory.

However, the bushcricket research supports an alternative hypothesis: that larger testicles permit a higher total number of mates rather than a higher sperm allocation per mate.

The study examined testicle sizes across 21 species of bushcrickets, finding wide variation in proportional testicle size before identifying Platycleis affinis as the record-breaker.

Dr Vahed emphasised the importance of not applying findings from vertebrates universally: "One important message is that we shouldn't expect that exactly the same rules and situations apply across all species; it can be an either-or."

# Ancient Egyptian Mummies Reveal Secrets Through Revolutionary CT Scanning

Never before has anyone seen mummy hair, muscles and bone in such detail. In a groundbreaking study, researchers at the British Museum have used cutting-edge technology to peer beneath the wrappings of ancient Egyptian mummies, revealing unprecedented insights into the lives and deaths of people who lived thousands of years ago.

Each mummy was put into a special CT scanner (an X-ray machine) to investigate the mummies layer by layer, building up a 3D picture of each one. The study's revealed many details about who these people were, how they lived and how they died.

By peeling away each layer museum staff could see the face of the person underneath the bandages and for the first time to tell the age of the mummies, what they ate, and the kinds of diseases they suffered from.

John Taylor, from the British Museum said he was "stunned" when he saw the images. "It's as if you switched a light on in a dark room and things jump out with a clarity where you are able to find out what the life experiences of these people really were," he said.

The researchers were able to see muscles and even arteries in the ancient bodies. They even saw that some arteries seemed clogged with fatty deposits, which could mean that these particular people ate rich fatty foods and maybe died of heart disease.

After peeling away the muscle, researchers were able to see the skeletons in amazing detail. They were able to guess the age of the individual mummies from their pelvis and their teeth. Many of them had bad teeth with signs of abscesses (infections), which would have been very painful to live with.

One scan shows a spatula left inside the mummy's skull. The tool would have been used to pull the brain out through the nostrils during the embalming process. But in this case a large chunk of brain was left inside, along with the tool, possibly because the person carrying out the embalming did a bad job.

Researchers also discovered that the mummies lived between 3,500BC and 700AD. All of them lived in the Nile Valley in Egypt.

# Scotland's Income Gap Narrows Despite Regional Disparities

Scotland's disposable income has grown faster than the UK average over the past 16 years, though significant regional variations remain, according to new research from the Scottish Parliament Information Centre.

The study revealed that Scotland's average disposable income in 2013 stood at £17,039 per head after tax and benefits, slightly below the UK average of £17,599. However, in real terms, Scottish incomes have risen by 27% since 1997, outpacing the 23% growth across the UK as a whole.

In cash terms, excluding inflation, Scottish income increased by 81% over the same period, compared with 75% for the entire UK. This demonstrates that the income gap between Scotland and the rest of the UK has narrowed considerably since 1997.

**Regional Variations**

The research highlighted stark differences across Scotland's regions. Only two areas – the north-east and Edinburgh – recorded disposable incomes exceeding £20,000 per head, placing them among the top 20% of UK regions.

Aberdeen and Aberdeenshire enjoyed the highest incomes, at 35% above Glasgow levels. However, these figures predate the recent slump in oil prices, which has significantly impacted the north-east economy.

At the other end of the scale, Glasgow recorded the lowest disposable income per head in Scotland. West central Scotland, West Lothian, and parts of Tayside also featured among the poorest areas, with Glasgow and North Lanarkshire falling into the bottom 25% for UK income.

The disparity between Scotland's richest and poorest areas exceeded £5,000 per head, highlighting persistent regional inequality.

**Benefits Dependency**

The analysis also examined the role of social benefits, including pensions and welfare payments, in household income. Benefits accounted for 21% of Scottish disposable income, slightly higher than the UK figure of just below 20%.

The west Highlands and Ayrshire emerged as Scotland's most benefit-dependent regions. The area encompassing Lochaber, Skye and Lochalsh, Arran and Cumbrae, along with Argyll and Bute, derived 28% of its income from benefits – placing it in the top 10% of UK regions for benefit reliance.

Areas with high concentrations of older people or greater poverty levels showed the highest dependency on benefits as income sources.

**Income Distribution**

Additional analysis from the Budget for Fiscal Responsibility, using HMRC statistics from 2012-13, revealed that Scotland's income tax-paying population is slightly more weighted towards lower earning segments compared to the UK average.

The most significant difference appeared among high earners, with Scotland having a notably smaller proportion of people earning more than £150,000 annually. However, Scotland's income distribution was much closer to the UK average than Wales's distribution.

# Northern Ireland's Corporation Tax Plan Loses Edge as UK Rate Drops

# Armed Police Debate Intensifies Following London Bridge Terror Attack

A former Royal Ulster Constabulary (RUC) Special Branch officer has called for all police officers in the UK to carry firearms following Saturday's terror attack in London, which left seven people dead and 48 injured.

William Matchett, who has also advised on policing matters in Iraq and Afghanistan and authored a book about Special Branch operations during the Northern Ireland Troubles, argues that the nature of modern terrorism requires a fundamentally different police response than what was needed during the Troubles.

"When you look at this new threat and the way it's manifested in England, particularly looking at vehicles, looking at cars and knives to kill people - it's very quick, it's very dynamic and it happens within seconds," Mr Matchett explained.

He drew a stark contrast between terrorist tactics in Northern Ireland and those employed in recent mainland UK attacks. "It's a totally different ball game to what I grew up with in Northern Ireland, where the terrorist essentially attacked someone. It was very short, it was sharp and then they looked to get away," he said.

"In England, in the last three series of attacks, that's not been the case - they actually hang about and try to kill as many people as possible."

Mr Matchett argued that the speed and brutality of these attacks necessitates immediate armed response. "So the quicker that it's stopped the better and, in that respect, it's very hard now to stand up against every police officer carrying a sidearm and that's through from your neighbourhood beat, your community officers, to plain clothes officers - that everyone on and off duty has a sidearm."

Commissioner Dick emphasized that neither the public nor police officers themselves are comfortable with universal arming. She also challenged the assumption that armed officers provide better protection, citing examples from France where armed lone officers have proven vulnerable.

"In other countries where you have someone armed with a sidearm who is going about his normal business as a community officer - they are also very, very vulnerable," she explained. "So to have people who can deal with this kind of very complex terrifying threat strikes me as the right way to go."
